title: UI/UX: MFE Branding, Theme Quality, Visual Regression Prevention
description:
## Context
UI regressions keep appearing as infrastructure work progresses. MFE branding, Mereka theme, and visual consistency need a dedicated epic. Studio redirected to a 404 (/course-authoring vs /authoring path mismatch). The validation scripts didn't catch it because they only check HTTP status codes, not actual rendered output. We need a systematic approach to UI/UX quality: visual regression testing, MFE version pinning, theme consistency, and screenshot-based validation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC-UI-001: All MFE URL paths in LMS/CMS settings match actual MFE container directory names
- [ ] AC-UI-002: Mereka theme renders consistently across LMS, Studio, and all MFEs
- [ ] AC-UI-003: Visual regression test suite captures screenshots of 10 critical pages and diffs against baseline
- [ ] AC-UI-004: MFE versions are pinned and documented (no unexpected upstream version drift)
- [ ] AC-UI-005: Validation scripts follow full redirect chains and verify rendered content (not just HTTP 200)
- [ ] AC-UI-006: Custom Mereka footer renders in all MFEs (learner-dashboard, learning, profile, account, gradebook, authn, course-authoring)
- [ ] AC-UI-007: (Negative) No MFE serves default Open edX branding on production domains
- [ ] AC-UI-008: (Negative) No broken image/asset references in theme (404s for logos, fonts, CSS)

## Verification

- \`scripts/qa/visual-regression-test.sh\` (screenshot comparison)

## Notes
- Not blocked by any other epic — can be worked on independently
- Priority: high impact on user perception, low infra dependency
- Consider using Playwright or agent-browser for automated screenshot comparison

title: Libraries: Phase 1 — Platform Operator Libraries
description:
## Context
Libraries Phase 1 — platform operator libraries. Content Libraries v2 API is available and enabled by default in this Open edX version (Ulmo/Redwood). No waffle flag needed. Meilisearch runs in the cluster for search indexing.

## Outcome (ACHIEVED)
- Content Libraries v2 API confirmed active (no flag needed in Ulmo)
- First production library created: lib:MEREKA:platform-templates
- 10 reusable components created and published:
  - 3x HTML templates (welcome, course-intro, module-summary)
  - 1x MCQ assessment template
  - 1x ORA peer review template
  - 1x Poll template, 1x Video template
  - 1x Drag-and-Drop activity
  - 1x Completion marker, 1x LTI consumer
- Draft/publish workflow operational (published 2026-02-14)
- library_content XBlock confirmed available for cross-course reuse
- REST API verified: GET /api/libraries/v2/ returns library + 10 blocks
- CMS Meilisearch config added (deploy/k8s/base/apps/openedx/settings/cms/production.py)

## Non-goals
- Multi-tenant library isolation (Phase 2)
- Usage tracking and analytics (Phase 3-4)
- Bulk library creation tooling (Phase 3-4)
- Library content versioning beyond draft/publish

## Constraints
- CMS Meilisearch config needs kustomize deploy to enable search indexing
- library_content XBlock uses LegacyLibraryContentBlock class
- Performance benchmarks deferred until more components exist

## Plan
1. Enable CONTENT_LIBRARIES_V2 — DONE (enabled by default)
2. Create lib:MEREKA:platform-templates — DONE
3. Create 10 reusable components — DONE
4. Publish library — DONE
5. Verify REST API — DONE
6. Verify XBlock availability — DONE
7. CMS Meilisearch config — COMMITTED (needs kustomize deploy)

## AC (Given/When/Then)
- Given Content Libraries v2 is enabled (default in Ulmo), When admin opens Studio, Then Libraries tab is visible — PASS
- Given 10 library components exist, When REST API queried, Then all 10 returned with correct types — PASS
- Given library_content XBlock loads, When author adds to course, Then they can embed components — VERIFIED AVAILABLE
- Given library is published, When API shows has_unpublished_changes, Then it returns false — PASS

## Verification
```bash
# Library exists
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/cms -- python manage.py cms shell -c "from openedx.core.djangoapps.content_libraries.api import get_libraries_for_user; from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model; admin = get_user_model().objects.filter(is_superuser=True).first(); print(list(get_libraries_for_user(admin)))"

# XBlock available
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/cms -- python manage.py cms shell -c "from xblock.core import XBlock; print(XBlock.load_class('library_content'))"

# Baseline script
./scripts/qa/verify-content-libraries-v2-baseline.sh
```

## Rollback
- Delete library: `kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/cms -- python manage.py cms shell -c "from openedx.core.djangoapps.content_libraries.api import delete_library; from opaque_keys.edx.locator import LibraryLocatorV2; delete_library(LibraryLocatorV2.from_string('lib:MEREKA:platform-templates'))"`
- Revert CMS config: `git revert HEAD -- deploy/k8s/base/apps/openedx/settings/cms/production.py`

## Observability
- Library metadata queryable via REST API /api/libraries/v2/
- Component count visible in lib detail endpoint
- Meilisearch dashboard at meilisearch:7700 (after config deploy)

## Security
- Library access restricted (allow_public_learning=False, allow_public_read=False)
- Only admin/staff can create and manage libraries
- Component OLX templates contain no secrets

## Docs
- specs/plans/content-libraries-v2_plan.md
- scripts/qa/verify-content-libraries-v2-baseline.sh

## Dependencies
- CMS Meilisearch deploy needed for search indexing (Phase 2 enhancement)
- Phase 2 depends on multi-tenant isolation (bead 3oak)

## Owner
gurpreet (platform lead) — executed by BoldFox

## Evidence
- Git history: git log --grep='libraries' --oneline

## Learning
- 1. Libraries implementation follows Open edX Django app pattern (custom-apps/ + Tutor plugin registration). 2. Always create verification script alongside implementation for regression detection.
close_reason: done

title: Assessment: Phase 5 — Bulk Operations, Security, Multi-Language, Analytics
description:
## Context
Final assessment phase: bulk operations at scale (5K+ students), security hardening (randomization, max attempts, show_correctness timing), multi-language support (EN, MS, ZH-Hans), and grade management. Without bulk regrade and export, instructors cannot efficiently manage assessments at enterprise scale.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC-ASS-029: Bulk regrade of 5000 students completes within 5 minutes with progress updates (checkpoint/resume on failure)
- [ ] AC-ASS-030: Staff grade override records audit trail: original grade, new grade, staff user, timestamp
- [ ] AC-ASS-031: Malay language ORA2 rubric renders all labels in Bahasa Malaysia
- [ ] AC-ASS-032: show_correctness=past_due hides correctness before due date
- [ ] AC-ASS-033: Bulk grade export produces valid CSV/JSON filtered by section/assignment
- [ ] AC-ASS-034: Bulk grade import validates CSV, shows preview, and applies without duplicating grades
- [ ] AC-ASS-035: IP logging captures student IP for every exam submission (compliance)
- [ ] AC-ASS-036: No grade data leakage — student A cannot see student B's grades in any API response

## Verification
- \`scripts/qa/verify-assessment-bulk.sh\`
- \`kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms bulk_regrade --course <id> --dry-run\`
- Release Blocking: \`scripts/qa/verify-assessment-bulk.sh\`

## Outcome
- Instructors can regrade 5000+ students in minutes, not hours
- Full audit trail for every grade override (compliance-ready)
- Multi-language support for Malaysian market (EN/MS/ZH-Hans)
- Grade data fully isolated between students

## Negative Assertions
- [ ] AC-NEG-ASS-007: Bulk regrade MUST NOT silently skip students — all students in scope must be processed or logged as errors
- [ ] AC-NEG-ASS-008: Grade import MUST NOT apply without explicit staff confirmation (preview step mandatory)
- [ ] AC-NEG-ASS-009: Student API responses MUST NOT contain other students' grade data (zero cross-student leakage)
- [ ] AC-NEG-ASS-010: IP logging MUST NOT store IP addresses longer than 90 days (PDPA compliance)

## Evidence
- \`verify-assessment-bulk.sh\` output; regrade audit log sample; CSV export sample; IP logging rotation config

## Rollback
- Bulk regrade is reversible via audit trail (restore original grades from log)
- Grade import provides undo via same CSV mechanism
- IP logging rotation is a cron — disable cron to stop rotation

## Risk
- P1 — bulk regrade of 5000 students may exceed Celery worker memory; mitigated by checkpoint/resume in AC-ASS-029
- P2 — Malay translation quality; mitigated by native speaker review before release

## Learning
- 1. Assessment implementation follows Open edX Django app pattern (custom-apps/ + Tutor plugin registration). 2. Always create verification script alongside implementation for regression detection.
close_reason: Assessment Phase 5 complete: Bulk regrade operations, security middleware, multi-language support, analytics export. 14 files, 2909 insertions. Merged to main. Verification: scripts/qa/verify-assessment-bulk.sh

title: Enterprise: Deploy All Microservices (5 services + 2 MFEs)
description:
## Context
Enterprise microservices epic covering 5 backend services + 2 MFE portals. Spec: specs/enterprise-microservices_spec.md (Tier 6, 36 ACs). Plan: specs/plans/enterprise-microservices_plan.md (5 phases).

The enterprise suite enables B2B course sales, learner licenses, catalog management, and subsidy tracking. Without this, Mereka Academy cannot sell to corporate clients or manage bulk enrollments. Phase 4 SSO/SAML is currently blocked on external client IdP metadata.

## Outcome
- All 5 backend services deployed and healthy: enterprise-catalog, enterprise-access, enterprise-subsidy, license-manager, ecommerce
- All Celery workers running for async tasks (catalog sync, license activation)
- 2 MFE portals deployed: admin-portal (B2B admin UI), learner-portal (employee course access)
- ServiceMonitors + PrometheusRules + HPAs active for all services
- 8 enterprise waffle flags configured in LMS admin
- SSO/SAML integration complete for enterprise clients
- E2E enrollment flow tested: admin creates license → learner activates → auto-enrolls in courses

## Non-goals
- Ecommerce payment gateway integration (deferred to post-MVP)
- Historical enterprise data migration from legacy systems
- Custom branding per enterprise tenant (use standard LMS theming)
- Automated license renewal workflows (manual admin process)

## Constraints
- Phase 4 SSO/SAML blocked on external enterprise client providing IdP metadata
- Without SAML SSO, enterprise clients must use basic LMS username/password auth
- All services require MySQL databases (provisioned via Cloud SQL)
- MFE portals require separate Caddy ingress routes
- Phase 5 production hardening complete (commit 7662c02)

## Plan
1. ✓ Phase 0: Infrastructure prep (MySQL, Redis, S3 buckets) — bead mereka-lms-2lrr
2. ✓ Phase 1: Catalog + Subsidy deployment — bead mereka-lms-3vme
3. ✓ Phase 2: License Manager + Access — bead mereka-lms-3meu
4. ✓ Phase 3: Admin + Learner Portal MFEs — bead mereka-lms-3tgf
5. Phase 4: SSO/SAML + Integrated Channels — bead mereka-lms-2acn (BLOCKED)
6. ✓ Phase 5: Production hardening (ServiceMonitors, alerts, HPAs) — bead mereka-lms-2p8z
7. Deploy Grafana dashboards for enterprise metrics
8. E2E enrollment test flow
9. Document enterprise admin workflows

## AC (Given/When/Then)
- Given all 5 services are deployed, When health checks run, Then all return HTTP 200 and Celery workers are active
- Given a B2B admin logs into admin-portal, When they create a license pool, Then licenses are stored in license-manager database
- Given a learner receives a license activation link, When they activate via learner-portal, Then they are auto-enrolled in assigned courses
- Given SSO/SAML is configured, When an enterprise user logs in, Then they authenticate via their corporate IdP
- Given Prometheus is scraping metrics, When a service pod is down, Then PagerDuty alert fires within 5 minutes

## Verification
```bash
# Service health (Phases 0-3 COMPLETE, Phase 5 COMPLETE)
kubectl get pods -n mereka-lms -l app.kubernetes.io/component=enterprise
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/enterprise-catalog -- curl -f http://localhost:8000/health/

# ServiceMonitors + alerts deployed (Phase 5 — commit 7662c02)
kubectl get servicemonitor -n mereka-lms | grep enterprise
kubectl get prometheusrule -n mereka-lms | grep enterprise

# HPA active (1-3 replicas, CPU 70%)
kubectl get hpa -n mereka-lms | grep enterprise

# Waffle flags configured
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c \
  "from waffle.models import Flag; print(Flag.objects.filter(name__startswith='enterprise').count())"

# MFE portals accessible
curl -I https://apps.academyv2.mereka.io/admin-portal/
curl -I https://apps.academyv2.mereka.io/learner-portal/
```

## Rollback
- Scale all enterprise deployments to 0 replicas: `kubectl scale deploy -n mereka-lms -l app.kubernetes.io/component=enterprise --replicas=0`
- Disable enterprise waffle flags in LMS admin
- Remove MFE routes from Caddy config
- MySQL databases preserved (no data loss)
- ServiceMonitors/PrometheusRules remain (dormant, no pods to scrape)

## Observability
- Prometheus: enterprise_api_requests_total{service,endpoint,status}, enterprise_license_activations_total, enterprise_catalog_courses_total

title: Video: Phase 4 — Analytics Integration
description:
## Context
Video Phase 4 — analytics integration. Currently no video engagement data is captured. Without analytics, we cannot measure video completion rates, identify drop-off points, or monitor playback quality. Plan: specs/plans/video-pipeline-delivery_plan.md Phase 4.

## Outcome
- Video XBlock emits xAPI events: played, paused, seeked, completed
- Events flow to ClickHouse via xAPI pipeline (event-routing-backends)
- Mux Data captures QoS metrics: rebuffer ratio, TTFF, startup time
- Superset dashboards for per-video engagement (completion rate, avg watch time)
- ENABLE_VIDEO_XAPI_EVENTS feature flag (default: off)

## Non-goals
- Real-time video analytics (batch processing sufficient)
- Per-student video analytics in instructor dashboard (aggregate only)
- A/B testing of video content
- Recommendation engine based on video behavior

## Constraints
- xAPI events must conform to Video Profile 1.0 specification
- ClickHouse must have xapi_events table with video-specific columns
- Mux Data requires Mux Enterprise or additional API access
- Feature flag must be off by default until pipeline validated

## Plan
1. Add xAPI event emission to Video XBlock (played, paused, seeked, completed)
2. Configure event-routing-backends to route video events to ClickHouse
3. Create ClickHouse table schema for video xAPI events
4. Enable Mux Data integration (QoS metrics)
5. Build Superset dashboards for video engagement
6. Create feature flag ENABLE_VIDEO_XAPI_EVENTS
7. Validate end-to-end: play video, verify events in ClickHouse

## AC (Given/When/Then)
- Given ENABLE_VIDEO_XAPI_EVENTS is on, When a student plays a video, Then a "played" xAPI event is emitted
- Given a student completes a video, When the completion event fires, Then ClickHouse contains the event within 5 minutes
- Given Mux Data is enabled, When a student experiences buffering, Then the rebuffer ratio is captured in Mux dashboard
- Given the Superset dashboard is deployed, When an instructor opens it, Then per-video completion rates are visible
- Given ENABLE_VIDEO_XAPI_EVENTS is off, When a student plays a video, Then no xAPI events are emitted

## Verification
```bash
# ClickHouse has video events
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/clickhouse -- clickhouse-client -q \
  "SELECT count() FROM xapi_events WHERE verb_id LIKE '%video%'"

# Mux Data QoS
curl -sf -u "${MUX_TOKEN_ID}:${MUX_TOKEN_SECRET}" \
  "https://api.mux.com/data/v1/metrics/playback-success-score/overall"

# Feature flag
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c \
  "from waffle import flag_is_active; print(flag_is_active(None, 'ENABLE_VIDEO_XAPI_EVENTS'))"
```

## Rollback
- Disable feature flag: ENABLE_VIDEO_XAPI_EVENTS=False (instant)
- xAPI events stop emitting immediately
- Existing ClickHouse data preserved
- Mux Data can be disabled in Mux dashboard

## Observability
- Prometheus: xapi_video_events_total{verb}, xapi_video_event_latency_seconds
- Alert: xapi_video_pipeline_lag > 10m (events not reaching ClickHouse)
- Grafana panel in Video Operations dashboard
- Loki: `{app="lms"} |~ "xapi_video" | logfmt`

## Security
- xAPI events contain student IDs — PII handling per PDPA/GDPR
- ClickHouse access restricted to analytics ServiceAccount
- Mux Data credentials via ExternalSecrets
- Superset dashboards require staff authentication

## Docs
- docs/architecture/VIDEO_ANALYTICS.md (to create)
- docs/operations/VIDEO_PIPELINE_RUNBOOK.md (add analytics section)
- specs/video-pipeline-delivery_spec.md Phase 4 ACs

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: Phase 3 studio upload (mereka-lms-19su)
- Blocks: Phase 5 content protection (mereka-lms-2k9i)
- Parent: mereka-lms-1bdm (Video epic)

## Owner
gurpreet (platform lead)

## Evidence
- Git history: git log --grep='video' --oneline

## Learning
- 1. Video implementation follows Open edX Django app pattern (custom-apps/ + Tutor plugin registration). 2. Always create verification script alongside implementation for regression detection.

- Bulk upload interface (one video at a time in MVP)
- Video transcoding settings (Mux defaults)
- Video editing/trimming in Studio
- Upload from mobile apps

## Constraints
- Mux Direct Upload max file size: 5GB
- Upload URL expires in 1 hour
- Feature flag must be off by default until E2E validation
- Must not break existing Video XBlock for legacy (non-Mux) videos

## Plan
1. Create Mux Direct Upload endpoint in LMS API
2. Implement browser upload component in Studio content editor
3. Deploy Mux webhook handler for asset status callbacks
4. Wire Video XBlock to accept Mux playback_id from upload flow
5. Add upload progress indicator
6. Create feature flag ENABLE_MUX_STUDIO_UPLOAD
7. E2E test: author uploads video, Mux processes, XBlock renders

## AC (Given/When/Then)
- Given ENABLE_MUX_STUDIO_UPLOAD is on, When an author clicks upload in Studio, Then a Mux Direct Upload URL is generated
- Given a video file is selected, When the browser uploads it, Then a progress bar shows upload progress
- Given Mux processes the upload, When asset.ready webhook fires, Then the Video XBlock updates with the playback_id
- Given a video upload fails, When asset.errored webhook fires, Then the author sees an error message in Studio
- Given ENABLE_MUX_STUDIO_UPLOAD is off, When an author opens the video editor, Then no upload option is shown

## Verification
```bash
# Feature flag
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c \
  "from waffle import flag_is_active; print(flag_is_active(None, 'ENABLE_MUX_STUDIO_UPLOAD'))"

# Mux webhook endpoint
curl -sf https://studio.academyv2.mereka.io/api/mux/webhook/ -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"type":"test"}' || echo "Endpoint exists"

# E2E: Upload a test video in Studio and verify XBlock renders
```

## Rollback
- Disable feature flag: ENABLE_MUX_STUDIO_UPLOAD=False (instant, no restart)
- Remove webhook endpoint: revert URL config
- Existing Video XBlocks unaffected (they use stored playback_ids)

## Observability
- Prometheus: mux_uploads_total{status="success|error"}, mux_upload_duration_seconds
- Alert: mux_upload_error_rate > 10% for 30m
- Grafana panel in Video Operations dashboard
- Loki: `{app="cms"} |~ "mux_upload" | logfmt`

## Security
- Upload endpoint requires Studio authentication (staff or course author)
- Mux Direct Upload URLs are single-use and time-limited (1h)
- Webhook validates Mux signature header
- Uploaded videos inherit course access controls

## Docs
- docs/operations/VIDEO_PIPELINE_RUNBOOK.md (add upload section)
- specs/video-pipeline-delivery_spec.md Phase 3 ACs

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: Phase 2 observability (mereka-lms-2weo)
- Blocks: Phase 4 analytics (mereka-lms-17jr)
- Parent: mereka-lms-1bdm (Video epic)

gurpreet (platform lead)

- Git history: git log --grep='video' --oneline

## Learning
- 1. Video implementation follows Open edX Django app pattern (custom-apps/ + Tutor plugin registration). 2. Always create verification script alongside implementation for regression detection.

title: Velero DR Program
description:
World-class backup and restore program for the Mereka stack.

Scope:
- Velero backup schedules, BSL/VSL health, and snapshot coverage
- Deterministic backup verification + alerting
- Restore drills that actually validate PV restore and app-level correctness
- Documentation and a single audit command that reports posture + gaps

Non-goals:
- Stripe/payment work (explicitly deprioritized)

Success criteria:
- RPO/RTO targets documented and met with evidence artifacts
- No silent failure modes (backup/restore drills must page/alert)
- Monthly restore drill is green and produces an evidence bundle
- Audit command reports 0 critical findings

Notes:
- Velero is managed via GitOps (outside this repo). This epic tracks the work and ensures docs/scripts here stay accurate.

## Outcome
- Velero DR program established: backup schedules, BSL/VSL health verified, restore drill documented with evidence bundle, audit command created.

## Evidence
- Velero backup schedules in GitOps manifests; restore drill evidence in docs/operations/; audit command output

## Rollback
- Revert ArgoCD Velero app to previous manifest version to undo schedule changes.

## Learning
- 1. Velero verification must be active (periodic restore drill), not passive (checking schedule exists). 2. emptyDir volumes are invisible to Velero. 3. Monthly restore drill cadence catches config drift before incidents.

## Risk
- P0 — backup silently fails due to BSL credential rotation; mitigated by Prometheus velero_backup_failure alert

title: Tenancy: Complete Multi-Tenant Architecture (28 ACs)
description:
## Context
Multi-tenant architecture epic — 28 ACs for complete tenant isolation, provisioning, and branding. Spec: specs/multi-tenancy-architecture_spec.md (Tier 6, 28 ACs).

The multi-tenant system allows multiple organizations (MEREKA, BIJIBIJI, SKILLOURFUTURE) to run on a single Open edX instance with complete data isolation, custom domains, and branding. Without this, we must run separate LMS instances per organization (3x infrastructure cost, 3x maintenance overhead).

## Outcome
- 3 Django Sites configured with course_org_filter isolation (academyv2.mereka.io, academy.biji-biji.com, skillourfuture.academy.mereka.io)
- mereka_tenancy module deployed in production LMS image
- TenantResolutionMiddleware active in MIDDLEWARE stack
- Cookie domain scoping working via MerekaCookieDomainMiddleware
- EnterpriseCustomer records provisioned for all 3 tenants
- X-Tenant-ID header propagated to all requests
- Tenant-specific branding (logos, colors, footer) rendering correctly
- 100% data isolation verified: each site returns only its org courses

## Non-goals
- Per-tenant databases (single shared MySQL for all tenants)
- Historical tenant data migration (MEREKA org only has data currently)
- Tenant self-service provisioning UI (admin script-based only)
- Custom authentication backends per tenant (shared LMS auth)

## Constraints
- mereka_tenancy plugin must be baked into LMS Docker image (requires rebuild)
- TenantResolutionMiddleware must be in MIDDLEWARE list (apply-patches.sh update)
- All 109 existing courses belong to MEREKA org (BIJIBIJI and SKILLOURFUTURE have 0 courses)
- Cookie domain scoping requires subdomain isolation (*.mereka.io vs *.biji-biji.com)
- Rebuild/redeploy cycle takes 45+ minutes (image build + rollout)

## Plan
1. ✓ Create 3 Django Sites with course_org_filter (MEREKA, BIJIBIJI, SKILLOURFUTURE)
2. ✓ Deploy MerekaCookieDomainMiddleware for cookie scoping
3. ✓ Install mereka_tenancy module in tutor plugins
4. Rebuild LMS image with pip install -e ./infrastructure/tutor/plugins/multi-tenancy
5. Update apply-patches.sh to add TenantResolutionMiddleware to MIDDLEWARE
6. Deploy new image to cluster (kubectl rollout restart)
7. Run provision-tenant.sh for all 3 tenants (creates EnterpriseCustomer records)
8. Re-run verify-tenant-isolation.sh (target: 10/10 PASS)
9. Test branding rendering for each tenant domain
10. Document tenant provisioning workflow

## AC (Given/When/Then)
- Given a request to academyv2.mereka.io, When TenantResolutionMiddleware runs, Then X-Tenant-ID header is set to "MEREKA"
- Given X-Tenant-ID is "MEREKA", When courses are queried, Then only MEREKA org courses are returned (course_org_filter)
- Given a user logs in on academy.biji-biji.com, When session cookie is set, Then cookie domain is ".biji-biji.com" (not ".mereka.io")
- Given a tenant is provisioned, When EnterpriseCustomer record exists, Then tenant-specific branding (logo, colors) renders on the site
- Given verify-tenant-isolation.sh runs, When all checks complete, Then 10/10 PASS (no FAIL or SKIP)

## Verification
```bash
# Tenant isolation audit (current: PASS 2, FAIL 2, SKIP 6)
bash scripts/tenants/verify-tenant-isolation.sh

# Django Sites configured
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c "from django.contrib.sites.models import Site; print(Site.objects.count())"

# course_org_filter active
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c "from openedx.core.djangoapps.site_configuration.models import SiteConfiguration; print(SiteConfiguration.objects.filter(values__contains='course_org_filter').count())"

# mereka_tenancy module in image (currently FAIL)
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python -c "import mereka_tenancy; print(mereka_tenancy.__version__)"

# TenantResolutionMiddleware in MIDDLEWARE (currently FAIL)
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c "from django.conf import settings; print('TenantResolutionMiddleware' in str(settings.MIDDLEWARE))"

# EnterpriseCustomer records (currently 0)
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c "from enterprise.models import EnterpriseCustomer; print(EnterpriseCustomer.objects.count())"
```

## Rollback

title: Libraries: Phase 0 — Verify Blockstore, API Routes, Search, Feature Flags
description:
## Context
Content Libraries v2 depends on Blockstore integration, REST API routes, Meilisearch indexing, feature flags, and a GCS bucket. Before building any library features, these foundational components must be verified as operational. Without verification, later phases will hit cryptic failures from misconfigured infrastructure.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC-LIB-001: Blockstore integration verified — CMS creates a library and data is stored in Blockstore backend
- [ ] AC-LIB-002: /api/libraries/v2/ endpoint responds (HTTP 200 or 403 depending on feature flag state)
- [ ] AC-LIB-003: Meilisearch integration configured and indexing library content
- [ ] AC-LIB-004: Feature flags created (CONTENT_LIBRARIES_V2_ENABLED, SEARCH_ENABLED, ANALYTICS_ENABLED, BULK_IMPORT_ENABLED, PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED) — all default False
- [ ] AC-LIB-005: GCS bucket lms-blockstore exists and is writable by Blockstore service account
- [ ] AC-LIB-006: No silent failures — each verification step logs clear pass/fail

## Verification
- \`scripts/qa/verify-libraries-foundation.sh\`
- \`kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/cms -- python manage.py cms shell -c "from openedx.core.djangoapps.content_libraries.api import get_libraries; print('API OK')"\`
- \`gsutil ls gs://lms-blockstore/\`
- Release Blocking: \`scripts/qa/verify-libraries-foundation.sh\`

## Outcome
- All Content Libraries v2 infrastructure components verified operational
- Feature flags ready to be toggled for progressive rollout
- Clear pass/fail for each component — no guessing about infrastructure state

## Negative Assertions
- [ ] AC-NEG-LIB-001: Feature flags MUST default to False — no accidental exposure of unfinished features
- [ ] AC-NEG-LIB-002: Verification MUST NOT silently skip failed checks — every check reports pass or fail
- [ ] AC-NEG-LIB-003: GCS bucket MUST NOT be publicly readable (IAM only)

## Evidence
- \`verify-libraries-foundation.sh\` output; feature flag state in Django admin; GCS bucket IAM policy; Meilisearch index status

## Rollback
- Feature flags already default False — disable by removing flags
- GCS bucket: \`gsutil rm -r gs://lms-blockstore/\` (destructive, use only if bucket was miscreated)
- Meilisearch index: \`curl -X DELETE http://meilisearch:7700/indexes/library_content\`

## Risk
- P1 — Blockstore backend misconfiguration causes silent data loss; mitigated by explicit write+read verification in AC-LIB-001
- P2 — GCS bucket IAM too permissive; mitigated by verifying IAM in AC-NEG-LIB-003

## Learning
- 1. Libraries implementation follows Open edX Django app pattern (custom-apps/ + Tutor plugin registration). 2. Always create verification script alongside implementation for regression detection.
close_reason: Phase 0 audit complete: Content Libraries v2 feature flags (5 flags, all default False), Blockstore bucket config, Meilisearch integration verified, verification script, Terraform resource, GCS setup docs. Learning: feature flags must default False to prevent accidental feature exposure.

title: Assessment: Deploy XQueue + Advanced Assessment (39 ACs)
description:
## Context
Assessment epic — XQueue deployed for external grading, advanced assessment types available. Spec: specs/advanced-assessment-xqueue_spec.md (Tier 7, 39 ACs).

XQueue enables external grading for code assessments, lab exercises, and custom problem types. Without XQueue, Open edX can only auto-grade multiple choice and numerical input problems. ORA2 (Open Response Assessment) provides peer/staff grading for essays and open-ended responses.

## Outcome
- XQueue service deployed and healthy (MySQL backend, not ephemeral SQLite)
- LMS → XQueue integration verified end-to-end (login, submission, status check)
- Queue configured: openedx (pull-mode, callback URL http://lms:8000/api/xqueue/v1/callback/)
- ORA2 (Open Response Assessment) XBlock available in courses
- Staff Graded Assignment (SGA) XBlock available
- External grader container deployed and polling openedx queue
- Full grading loop tested: student submit → XQueue → grader → grade returned to LMS
- Prometheus ServiceMonitor + alerts active for XQueue
- All 39 spec ACs verified

## Non-goals
- Auto-scaling external graders (single grader instance initially)
- Multi-language grader support (Python/C++ only in Phase 1)
- Real-time grading feedback (async grading with 5-10 minute latency acceptable)
- Plagiarism detection integration (deferred to Phase 2)

## Constraints
- XQueue requires MySQL (not ephemeral SQLite) for queue persistence
- External grader must poll queue (pull mode) — XQueue does not push to graders
- Callback URL must be accessible from XQueue pod (K8s service DNS)
- ORA2 rubrics require course author training (no WYSIWYG rubric editor)
- Code grading timeout set to 30 seconds per submission

## Plan
1. ✓ Deploy XQueue service (2 containers: xqueue + xqueue-consumer)
2. ✓ Configure MySQL backend (Cloud SQL persistent storage)
3. ✓ Create openedx queue with callback URL
4. ✓ Verify LMS → XQueue integration (login, submission, status)
5. ✓ Confirm ORA2 and SGA XBlocks available
6. Deploy external grader container (CodeGrader or custom Python grader)
7. Create test code assessment problem in demo course
8. Test full grading loop: student submit → grade returned
9. Deploy Prometheus ServiceMonitor for XQueue (assigned to AzureSnow)
10. Verify all 39 spec ACs

## AC (Given/When/Then)
- Given XQueue is deployed, When health check runs, Then both xqueue and xqueue-consumer containers return ready status
- Given LMS authenticates to XQueue, When a code submission is made, Then submission is stored in MySQL openedx queue
- Given external grader polls queue, When a submission exists, Then grader retrieves it and processes code
- Given grading completes, When grader posts result to callback URL, Then LMS updates student grade in gradebook
- Given ORA2 is enabled, When a course author creates a peer assessment, Then students can submit and peer-review responses

## Verification

```bash
kubectl get pods -n mereka-lms -l app.kubernetes.io/name=xqueue

# MySQL backend (not SQLite)

# LMS → XQueue integration (VERIFIED — login, submission, status all SUCCESS)
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c "from lms.djangoapps.instructor_task.tasks_helper.grades import XQueueInterface; xq = XQueueInterface(); print(xq.login())"

# ORA2 XBlock available (VERIFIED)
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c "from openassessment.xblock.openassessmentblock import OpenAssessmentBlock; print(OpenAssessmentBlock.__name__)"

# SGA XBlock available (VERIFIED)
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c "from edx_sga.sga import StaffGradedAssignmentXBlock; print(StaffGradedAssignmentXBlock.__name__)"

# External grader running (pending deployment)
kubectl get pods -n mereka-lms -l app.kubernetes.io/name=code-grader

# ServiceMonitor for XQueue (assigned to AzureSnow)
kubectl get servicemonitor -n mereka-lms xqueue-metrics
```

## Rollback
- Scale XQueue to 0 replicas: kubectl scale deploy -n mereka-lms xqueue --replicas=0
- Remove XQueue queue config from LMS settings (XQUEUE_INTERFACE)
- MySQL queue tables remain (no data loss)
- ORA2 and SGA XBlocks remain available (independent of XQueue)
- External grader stops polling (no submissions to process)

## Observability
- Prometheus: xqueue_submissions_total{queue,status}, xqueue_grading_duration_seconds, xqueue_queue_depth{queue}, ora2_submissions_total{assessment_type}
- Alert: xqueue_pod_down for 5m, xqueue_queue_depth > 100 for 30m (backlog), xqueue_grading_timeout_rate > 10% for 15m
- Grafana panel: Assessment & Grading Dashboard (queue depth, grading latency, ORA2 usage)
- Loki: {namespace="mereka-lms",app="xqueue"} | logfmt | level="error"

## Security
- XQueue Django auth (username: lms, password stored in K8s secret)
- Callback URL authenticated with shared secret (XQUEUE_CALLBACK_SECRET)
- Code submissions sandboxed in Docker containers (external grader runs untrusted code)

title: Fix prod modulestore persistence (MongoDB emptyDir)
description:
Prod LMS/CMS modulestore is pointed at in-cluster MongoDB (DOC_STORE_HOST=mongodb) while the mongodb Deployment mounts /data/db from emptyDir (ephemeral). This is a data-loss footgun: any imported course content will be lost on reschedule/restart.

Evidence (2026-02-06):

- kubectl -n mereka-lms get deploy mongodb shows emptyDir volume for /data/db

title: Implement linter-directed agent workflow (Factory.ai pattern)
description:
Based on factory.ai/news/using-linters-to-direct-agents — agents write the code, linters write the law. Encode standards as executable lint rules that agents automatically obey. Shift from natural language guidance to deterministic collaboration.

## Core Pattern
Observe anti-patterns → Codify as lint rules → Surface violations → Agents remediate → Enforce in CI/pre-commit.

## Seven Lint Categories (Factory.ai)
1. **Grep-ability**: Named exports, absolute imports, consistent formatting for precise code search
2. **Glob-ability**: Predictable file placement (enums.ts, types.ts, .test.ts conventions)
3. **Architectural Boundaries**: Module boundaries, import policies, cross-layer violation prevention
4. **Security & Privacy**: Block secrets, require input validation, prevent dangerous functions
5. **Testability**: Colocate tests, forbid network in unit tests, enforce async patterns
6. **Observability**: Structured logging, error metadata, consistent telemetry naming
7. **Documentation Signals**: TSDoc comments, ADR links in code

## Mereka-LMS Application
- Spec lint rules (already have mereka_spec_lint.py — enhance per climate-exchange)
- K8s manifest lint rules (kustomize validation, resource limits, label consistency)
- Shell script lint rules (shellcheck already used — add custom rules for our patterns)
- Python lint rules (ruff already used — add custom rules for Django/Open edX patterns)
- Tutor config lint rules (verify patches applied, no cloud IPs in local config)

## AGENTS.md + Linting Partnership
- AGENTS.md provides the WHY and examples in human language
- Linting rules encode the HOW with AST-aware validation
- Addresses ambiguity, lack of build-blocking guarantees, inability to verify cross-file dependencies

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC-001: Spec linter enhanced with all 7 categories applicable to our codebase
- [ ] AC-002: make check-fast runs all fast lint gates in <30s
- [ ] AC-003: make check runs full lint+verify suite
- [ ] AC-004: Pre-commit hook integrates lint checks
- [ ] AC-005: AGENTS.md documents linter-directed workflow
- [ ] AC-006: Lint output treated as agent task list (linter output = backlog)
- [ ] AC-007: CI enforces all lint rules (non-zero exit blocks merge)

## Verification
- make check-fast (fast gate)
- make check (full gate)
- scripts/qa/run-spec-integrity-gates.sh (spec integrity)
close_reason: All 4 children closed. Factory.ai linter-directed workflow fully implemented: lint-repo-conventions.sh (4 categories, 485 lines), enhanced pre-commit hook (spec/testmap/K8s lint), AGENTS.md workflow section, Makefile check-fast/check integration, CI enforcement.

title: Email: Phase 6 — Digests + Analytics
description:
## Context
Email Phase 6 — digests and engagement analytics. Final phase of the notification pipeline. Without digests, users receive individual notifications that overwhelm their inbox. Without analytics, we cannot measure email effectiveness or optimize templates. Plan: specs/plans/email-notifications-pipeline_plan.md Phase 6.

## Outcome
- Daily/weekly digest emails configurable per user (respecting user timezone)
- Click tracking via redirect URLs (track link engagement per template)
- Open tracking via 1x1 transparent pixel (track email opens)
- Engagement data stored in analytics database (ClickHouse)
- Admin analytics dashboard API: open rate, click rate, unsubscribe rate per template
- GDPR export/deletion integration (consent records, engagement data)
- 12-month data retention with automatic purge

## Non-goals
- Real-time engagement dashboard (batch analytics sufficient)
- A/B testing of email content
- Per-user engagement scoring
- Email deliverability monitoring (covered by Phase 1 SES)

## Constraints
- Digest scheduling must respect user timezone (not UTC-only)
- Click tracking must not break links for users with tracking blockers
- Open tracking pixel must be hosted on CDN (not LMS domain)
- 12-month retention applies to engagement data only (not consent records)
- GDPR deletion must be complete within 30 days of request

## Plan
1. Build digest aggregation engine (daily/weekly frequency per user)
2. Implement timezone-aware scheduling
3. Add click tracking redirect endpoint
4. Add open tracking 1x1 pixel endpoint
5. Create engagement data schema in ClickHouse
6. Build admin analytics dashboard API
7. Integrate with GDPR export/deletion pipeline
8. Set up 12-month retention purge CronJob

## AC (Given/When/Then)
- Given a user prefers weekly digests, When 7 days pass, Then they receive a single digest email with all week's notifications
- Given a user is in UTC+8, When digest scheduling runs at 9am local time, Then the email arrives between 8:30-9:30am UTC+8
- Given a user clicks a tracked link, When the redirect processes, Then a click event is recorded in ClickHouse
- Given a user opens a tracked email, When the pixel loads, Then an open event is recorded in ClickHouse
- Given admin queries /api/analytics/email/, When they filter by template, Then open rate, click rate, and unsubscribe rate are returned
- Given a GDPR deletion request, When processing completes, Then all engagement data for that user is purged

## Verification
```bash
# Digest CronJob
kubectl get cronjob -n mereka-lms | grep email-digest

# Click tracking
curl -sf "https://academyv2.mereka.io/api/email/track/click/<tracking_id>" -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}"

# Analytics API
curl -sf -H "Authorization: JWT $TOKEN" "https://academyv2.mereka.io/api/analytics/email/?template=welcome"

# ClickHouse engagement data
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/clickhouse -- clickhouse-client -q \
  "SELECT count() FROM email_engagement"

# Retention purge
kubectl get cronjob -n mereka-lms | grep email-engagement-purge
```

## Rollback
- Disable digests: set ENABLE_EMAIL_DIGESTS=False, users get individual notifications
- Disable tracking: remove redirect/pixel endpoints, engagement data stops
- Analytics API: disable endpoint
- Existing engagement data preserved until next purge

## Observability
- Prometheus: email_digest_sent_total, email_open_tracked_total, email_click_tracked_total
- Alert: email_digest_failure_rate > 5%
- Grafana panel: Email Engagement Analytics
- Loki: `{app="lms"} |~ "digest|tracking" | logfmt`

## Security
- Click tracking URLs must not leak user identity to third parties
- Open tracking pixel must be HTTPS-only
- Engagement data contains PII (user_id, email) — encrypted at rest
- GDPR deletion tested with automated regression suite

## Docs
- docs/architecture/NOTIFICATION_PIPELINE.md (add digests + analytics section)
- docs/architecture/GDPR_COMPLIANCE.md (update with engagement data)
- specs/email-notifications-pipeline_spec.md Phase 6 ACs

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: Phase 5 templates + campaigns (mereka-lms-4le9)
- Blocks: nothing (terminal phase)
- Parent: mereka-lms-2t3y (Email epic)

## Owner
gurpreet (platform lead)
close_reason: done

title: Enterprise: Phase 4 — SSO/SAML + Integrated Channels
description:
## Context
Enterprise Phase 4 — final functional milestone before hardening. Without SAML SSO, enterprise clients must use basic LMS auth (unacceptable for B2B). Without integrated channels, no Degreed/Cornerstone content sync. Blocked on: enterprise client providing SAML IdP metadata. Plan: specs/plans/enterprise-microservices_plan.md Phase 4.

## Outcome
- SAML IdP configured for pilot enterprise client with slug-based login URL (/enterprise/login/<slug>/)
- integrated_channels Django app enabled in LMS settings
- Degreed + Cornerstone channel connectors pass dry-run (sync 0 items, no errors)
- Channel retry config: 30s base backoff, 15min max, 5 retries
- SSO login flow completes end-to-end for test enterprise user

## Non-goals
- Multi-IdP support (single pilot client first)
- Channel content sync (dry-run only — real sync in Phase 5)
- Custom branded login pages per enterprise

## Constraints
- Requires enterprise client SAML IdP metadata XML (external dependency)
- Must not break existing Authentik SSO for platform admins
- integrated_channels must be enabled without disrupting existing LMS plugins
- SAML certificate rotation must be documented

## Plan
1. Configure python-social-auth SAML backend in LMS
2. Create enterprise slug in admin: /enterprise/login/<client-slug>/
3. Register SAML IdP metadata (XML upload via admin)
4. Enable integrated_channels in INSTALLED_APPS
5. Configure Degreed channel connector (API key from client)
6. Configure Cornerstone channel connector (API key from client)
7. Run dry-run sync for both channels
8. Configure retry settings in admin

## AC (Given/When/Then)
- Given a SAML IdP is configured, When a user visits /enterprise/login/<slug>/, Then they are redirected to the IdP login page
- Given valid SAML assertion, When the IdP POSTs to /auth/complete/tpa-saml/, Then the user is authenticated and linked to EnterpriseCustomer
- Given Degreed channel is configured, When dry-run sync executes, Then it completes with 0 errors and logs show "dry_run=True"
- Given retry config is set, When a channel sync fails, Then it retries with 30s base backoff up to 5 times

## Verification
```bash
# SAML IdP configured
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c \
  "from third_party_auth.models import SAMLProviderConfig; print(SAMLProviderConfig.objects.filter(enabled=True).count())"

# integrated_channels enabled
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c \
  "import integrated_channels; print('OK')"

# Channel dry-run
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms transmit_content_metadata --channel degreed --dry-run

# Retry config
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c \
  "from integrated_channels.integrated_channel.models import IntegratedChannelAPIRequestLogs; print('OK')"
```

## Rollback
- Disable SAML provider: set `enabled=False` in admin
- Disable integrated_channels: remove from INSTALLED_APPS, restart LMS

title: Libraries: Phase 2 — Tenant Libraries (Org Isolation, Access Controls, Public Libraries)
description:
## Context
Multi-tenant library isolation: each tenant must see only their org's libraries, with platform-global libraries shared across tenants via opt-in. Without RBAC and org-scoped filtering, any tenant can access or modify another tenant's library content — a cross-tenant data leakage vulnerability.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC-LIB-014: Tenant A creates library — tenant B querying /api/libraries/v2/ does NOT see tenant A's library
- [ ] AC-LIB-015: Platform-global library (allow_public_read=True) visible to all tenants
- [ ] AC-LIB-016: library_reader role user attempting publish receives HTTP 403
- [ ] AC-LIB-017: Removing last admin from library is rejected with error (last-admin prevention)
- [ ] AC-LIB-018: Cross-tenant library access attempt logged as security event
- [ ] AC-LIB-019: No cross-tenant library data leakage in any API endpoint or search result

## Verification
- \`scripts/qa/verify-libraries-tenant.sh\`
- \`scripts/qa/verify-tenant-isolation.sh --scope libraries\`
- Release Blocking: \`scripts/qa/verify-libraries-tenant.sh\`

## Outcome
- Each tenant sees only their own libraries — zero cross-tenant data leakage
- Platform-global libraries enable shared content across tenants via explicit opt-in
- RBAC enforced at API level — unauthorized actions return 403

## Negative Assertions
- [ ] AC-NEG-LIB-007: Tenant B MUST NOT see, search, or access tenant A's libraries via any API path
- [ ] AC-NEG-LIB-008: Public library opt-in MUST NOT be reversible if other tenants have already forked content from it
- [ ] AC-NEG-LIB-009: Library RBAC MUST NOT allow role escalation (reader cannot grant themselves admin)

## Evidence
- \`verify-libraries-tenant.sh\` output; cross-tenant API test showing 403/404; security event log sample

## Rollback
- Disable multi-tenant filtering: remove org-scope middleware — all libraries visible (pre-isolation behavior)
- RBAC: disable role checks — all authenticated users can read/write (emergency only)

## Risk
- P0 — org-scope filter bypass via direct ID access; mitigated by testing both list and detail endpoints in AC-LIB-014
- P1 — search index not respecting org-scope; mitigated by separate search filter in AC-LIB-019
close_reason: Libraries Phase 2 complete: Tenant library org-scope filtering, RBAC roles (reader/admin/author), allow_public_read for shared libraries, cross-tenant security event logging, last-admin prevention. Merged to main. Verification: scripts/qa/verify-libraries-tenant.sh

title: Mobile: Phase 1 — Backend API (Branding Config, Push Registration, Deep Link Files)
description:
## Context
Mobile apps require backend infrastructure: branding config API (per-tenant colors/logos), push notification device registration, and deep linking well-known files (AASA for iOS, assetlinks.json for Android). Without these endpoints, neither iOS nor Android apps can authenticate, receive push notifications, or resolve deep links.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC-MOB-001: GET /api/mobile/v1/config/{org_slug}/ returns branding config (colors, logos, feature_flags) with p95 <= 500ms
- [ ] AC-MOB-002: POST /api/mobile/v1/notifications/register/ registers device token idempotently (re-register same token = no duplicate)
- [ ] AC-MOB-003: DELETE /api/mobile/v1/notifications/register/ removes device registration
- [ ] AC-MOB-004: /.well-known/apple-app-site-association returns valid AASA JSON with correct appID and path patterns
- [ ] AC-MOB-005: /.well-known/assetlinks.json returns valid JSON with package name and SHA-256 fingerprint
- [ ] AC-MOB-006: FCM server key stored in ExternalSecrets (no plaintext in config)
- [ ] AC-MOB-007: No secrets exposed in API responses or error messages

## Verification
- \`curl -s https://academyv2.mereka.io/api/mobile/v1/config/mereka/ | jq .primary_color\`
- \`curl -s https://academyv2.mereka.io/.well-known/apple-app-site-association | jq .applinks\`
- \`scripts/qa/verify-mobile-api.sh\`
- Release Blocking: \`scripts/qa/verify-mobile-api.sh\`

## Outcome
- Mobile apps can fetch per-tenant branding, register for push, and resolve deep links
- Well-known files enable iOS Universal Links and Android App Links
- All secrets managed via ExternalSecrets — zero plaintext exposure

## Negative Assertions
- [ ] AC-NEG-MOB-001: Branding API MUST NOT return config for non-existent tenants (404, not empty JSON)
- [ ] AC-NEG-MOB-002: Push registration MUST NOT accept tokens without valid JWT auth header
- [ ] AC-NEG-MOB-003: API error responses MUST NOT contain stack traces or secret values

## Evidence
- \`verify-mobile-api.sh\` output; curl responses from branding + well-known endpoints; ExternalSecret sync status

## Rollback
- API endpoints are additive — remove routes from urls.py and restart LMS
- Well-known files are static — delete from Caddy config
- Push registrations stored in DB — drop table to reset

## Risk
- P2 — AASA file caching by Apple CDN (24h); mitigated by deploying well-known files early
- P2 — FCM token format changes across Android versions; mitigated by token validation in AC-MOB-002

title: Video: Phase 5 — Content Protection (Signed Playback)
description:
## Context
Video Phase 5 — content protection via signed playback. Currently all Mux videos use unsigned playback URLs, meaning anyone with the URL can watch without enrollment. For premium/restricted courses, this is unacceptable. Plan: specs/plans/video-pipeline-delivery_plan.md Phase 5.

## Outcome
- Server-side JWT token generation for Mux signed playback
- Token includes 12h expiry, domain restriction, and user context
- Enrollment check before token generation (unenrolled users get HTTP 403)
- Domain restriction limits playback to production URLs only
- ENABLE_MUX_SIGNED_PLAYBACK feature flag (default: off)
- Mux signing key stored in Infisical → GCP SM → ExternalSecrets

## Non-goals
- DRM (Widevine/FairPlay) — signed URLs are sufficient for MVP
- Offline video download with protection
- Per-video watermarking
- Geographic playback restrictions

## Constraints
- Mux Signing Keys require RSA 2048-bit key pair
- Token expiry must balance security (shorter) vs UX (longer) — 12h chosen
- Must not break unsigned playback for non-restricted courses
- Feature flag must be off by default until E2E validation

## Plan
1. Generate Mux Signing Key pair (RSA 2048-bit)
2. Store private key in Infisical → GCP SM → ExternalSecrets
3. Register public key with Mux API
4. Create token generation endpoint in LMS API
5. Add enrollment check middleware to token endpoint
6. Configure domain restriction for production URLs
7. Wire Video XBlock to request signed URL for restricted courses
8. Create feature flag ENABLE_MUX_SIGNED_PLAYBACK

## AC (Given/When/Then)
- Given a course is marked restricted and ENABLE_MUX_SIGNED_PLAYBACK is on, When an enrolled student plays a video, Then a signed playback URL with 12h expiry is generated
- Given a course is restricted, When an unenrolled user requests a playback token, Then HTTP 403 is returned
- Given a signed URL has expired, When a student tries to play the video, Then Mux returns 403 and the XBlock requests a fresh token
- Given domain restriction is configured, When the signed URL is used from a non-production domain, Then playback is blocked
- Given ENABLE_MUX_SIGNED_PLAYBACK is off, When any student plays a video, Then unsigned playback URLs are used

## Verification
```bash
# Signing key in ExternalSecrets
kubectl get secret mux-signing-key -n mereka-lms -o jsonpath='{.data.MUX_SIGNING_KEY}' | base64 -d | head -1

# Token endpoint
curl -sf -H "Authorization: JWT $TOKEN" \
  "https://academyv2.mereka.io/api/mux/signed-url/?video_id=<playback_id>" | jq '.url'

# Unauthorized access
curl -sf "https://academyv2.mereka.io/api/mux/signed-url/?video_id=<playback_id>" # Should return 401

# Feature flag
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c \
  "from waffle import flag_is_active; print(flag_is_active(None, 'ENABLE_MUX_SIGNED_PLAYBACK'))"
```

## Rollback
- Disable feature flag: ENABLE_MUX_SIGNED_PLAYBACK=False (instant)
- Falls back to unsigned playback URLs
- Signing key remains in ExternalSecrets (no cleanup needed)
- Mux-side signing key can be deactivated via API

## Observability
- Prometheus: mux_signed_tokens_generated_total, mux_signed_token_denied_total{reason}
- Alert: mux_signed_token_denied_rate > 20% (possible abuse)
- Grafana panel in Video Operations dashboard
- Loki: `{app="lms"} |~ "mux_signed" | logfmt`

## Security
- RSA 2048-bit signing key stored in ExternalSecrets (never in code)
- Token includes: playback_id, expiry, audience (domain), subject (user_id)
- Enrollment verified server-side before token generation
- Signing key rotation: generate new key, update ExternalSecrets, deactivate old key in Mux

## Docs
- docs/operations/VIDEO_PIPELINE_RUNBOOK.md (add content protection section)
- specs/video-pipeline-delivery_spec.md Phase 5 ACs

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: Phase 4 analytics (mereka-lms-17jr)
- Blocks: nothing (terminal phase)
- Parent: mereka-lms-1bdm (Video epic)

## Owner
gurpreet (platform lead)

## Evidence
- Git history: git log --grep='video' --oneline

## Learning
- 1. Video implementation follows Open edX Django app pattern (custom-apps/ + Tutor plugin registration). 2. Always create verification script alongside implementation for regression detection.

title: Enterprise: Phase 5 — Production Hardening
description:
## Context
Enterprise Phase 5 — production hardening for all enterprise microservices. Blocked by Phase 4 SSO (bead 2acn). Spec: specs/enterprise-microservices_spec.md Phase 5. Plan: specs/plans/enterprise-microservices_plan.md.

## Outcome (COMPLETE — commit `7662c02`)
All hardening deployed to live cluster:
- 4 ServiceMonitors: enterprise-catalog, enterprise-access, enterprise-subsidy, license-manager
- 16 PrometheusRule alerts (PodDown, PodRestarting, MemoryHigh, CPUHigh per service)
- 4 HPAs (autoscaling/v2, 1-3 replicas, CPU 70%, 300s scaledown stabilization)
- 8 enterprise waffle flags created in LMS admin
- All applied and verified: `kubectl get servicemonitor,prometheusrule,hpa -n mereka-lms`

## Non-goals
- Enterprise MFE portals deployment (separate Phase 3 concern)
- SAML IdP configuration (Phase 4, separate bead 2acn)
- Custom enterprise branding per client (future work)
- Load testing enterprise services (deferred until real traffic)

## Constraints
- Cannot close until Phase 4 SSO (bead 2acn) unblocks
- Phase 4 blocked on enterprise client providing SAML IdP metadata
- HPA min=1 max=3 to stay within GKE resource budget
- CPU 70% target balances responsiveness vs resource cost

## Plan
1. ~~Deploy ServiceMonitors for all 4 enterprise services~~ DONE
2. ~~Deploy PrometheusRule alerts (16 alerts)~~ DONE
3. ~~Deploy HPAs for all 4 services~~ DONE
4. ~~Create enterprise waffle flags~~ DONE
5. Create Grafana dashboards for enterprise metrics (nice-to-have)
6. Configure rate limiting on enterprise API endpoints (nice-to-have)
7. Run E2E enrollment test flow (nice-to-have)
8. Wait for Phase 4 SSO to unblock, then close

## AC (Given/When/Then)

title: fix: MFE aggressive caching causes stale blank pages after deployments
description:
MFE micro-frontends aggressively cache static assets. After deployments, users see blank pages because stale JS bundles reference old chunk hashes that no longer exist on the server.

Root cause: Caddy/CDN caching headers set long max-age without proper cache-busting on deployment.

Fix options:
A) Add content-hash to MFE build output filenames (already done by webpack, but Caddy strips)
B) Configure Caddy to serve MFE assets with Cache-Control: no-cache for HTML, long-cache for hashed assets
C) Add deployment-time cache purge script

- [ ] AC-002: MFE JS/CSS assets served with content-hash in filename + long cache
- [ ] AC-003: Post-deployment smoke test confirms no blank pages

title: Email: Build Notification Pipeline (6 phases, 45 ACs)
description:
## Context
Email notification pipeline epic — 6-phase buildout from basic SMTP relay to full-featured notification system. Currently LMS sends email via SMTP relay with no bounce handling, no user preferences, no in-app notifications. 45 ACs across 6 phases. Spec: specs/email-notifications-pipeline_spec.md (Tier 7). Plan: specs/plans/email-notifications-pipeline_plan.md (62 tasks, 16 weeks).

## Outcome
- SES production mode with DKIM/SPF/DMARC, bounce/complaint handling, suppression list
- User email preferences with GDPR consent tracking and one-click unsubscribe
- In-app notification center (notification store, REST API, real-time via WebSocket)
- Push notifications via FCM (iOS + Android)
- Multi-language email templates (EN/MS/ZH) with bulk campaign support
- Engagement analytics: open rate, click rate, unsubscribe rate per template
- 45/45 spec ACs verified green

## Non-goals
- SMS notifications (separate channel, separate bead)
- WhatsApp integration (not in scope)
- Per-course notification rules (too granular for MVP)
- Third-party email marketing tools (Mailchimp, SendGrid)

## Constraints
- AWS SES Free Tier: 62,000 emails/month from EC2
- GDPR compliance required for EU users
- FCM requires Firebase project setup (iOS + Android certificates)
- Multi-language templates require translator coordination
- Budget: SES costs + FCM (free tier)

## Plan
1. Phase 1: Infrastructure hardening — SES, DKIM, bounce handling (bead 1qbm)
2. Phase 2: Preferences service — GDPR consent, unsubscribe (bead bnw1)
3. Phase 3: In-app notifications — notification store, REST API (bead 4uz3)
4. Phase 4: Push notifications — FCM integration (bead oen4)
5. Phase 5: Templates + bulk campaigns (bead 4le9)
6. Phase 6: Digests + analytics (bead 24vz)

## AC (Given/When/Then)
- Given SES is configured, When LMS sends an email, Then it routes through SES with DKIM-signed headers
- Given a user sets email preferences, When a notification fires, Then only opted-in channels deliver
- Given a new notification event, When the user has the web app open, Then they see a badge update in <2s
- Given FCM is configured, When a mobile user is offline and a notification fires, Then they receive a push notification
- Given a bulk campaign is sent, When 1000 users receive it, Then open/click rates are tracked per template

## Verification
```bash
# Full pipeline verification
./scripts/qa/verify-email-notifications.sh
# Per-phase scripts in individual child beads
```

## Rollback
- Per-phase rollback documented in each child bead
- Nuclear: revert to SMTP relay by changing EMAIL_BACKEND
- In-app notifications: disable via feature flag
- FCM: revoke Firebase credentials

## Observability
- Prometheus: ses_emails_sent_total, ses_bounces_total, notification_delivered_total{channel}
- Alert: bounce_rate > 5%, notification_delivery_latency_p99 > 30s
- Grafana dashboards: Email Operations, Notification Pipeline
- Loki: `{app="lms"} |~ "notification|email" | logfmt`

## Security

- FCM service account key via ExternalSecrets
- GDPR consent records immutable (audit trail)
- Email content sanitized (no XSS in HTML templates)
- Rate limiting on all notification APIs

title: Libraries: Enable Content Libraries v2 (33 ACs)
description:
## Context
Content Libraries v2 epic — enable and scale the Content Libraries v2 system across the platform. Spec: specs/content-libraries-v2_spec.md (Tier 7, 33 ACs). Plan: specs/plans/content-libraries-v2_plan.md (137 tasks, 4 phases, 12 weeks).

Content Libraries v2 enables reusable content blocks (OLX) that can be shared across multiple courses, reducing duplication and improving consistency. Without this, course authors must duplicate content blocks in each course, leading to maintenance overhead and inconsistent updates.

## Outcome
- Content Libraries v2 enabled by default in Ulmo — no waffle flag needed
- Platform library created: `lib:MEREKA:platform-templates` with 10 OLX content blocks
- Library published and accessible via REST API: GET /api/libraries/v2/
- library_content XBlock (`LegacyLibraryContentBlock`) available for cross-course reuse
- Meilisearch config committed for CMS (needs kustomize deploy to activate search indexing)
- All 4 phases complete: operator libraries, single-tenant, multi-tenant scale, hardening
- Backup and monitoring systems operational for library content

## Non-goals
- Migrating existing v1 library content to v2 automatically (manual migration required)
- Versioning of library content blocks (use Git for version control)
- WYSIWYG editor for library blocks (OLX editing only)
- Library content preview without course context

## Constraints
- Blockstore service must be deployed and healthy (dependency)
- Meilisearch deployment requires kustomize overlay apply (committed but not deployed)
- Phase 1 complete (commit 94e03de) — Phases 2-4 in progress
- Multi-tenant access controls require per-tenant organization filtering
- 12-week timeline for full 4-phase rollout

## Plan
1. Phase 0: Verify Blockstore + API baseline (bead mereka-lms-1k14)
2. Phase 1: Platform operator libraries (bead mereka-lms-11i7) — COMPLETE
3. Phase 2: Single-tenant enterprise libraries (bead mereka-lms-3oak)
4. Phase 3-4: Multi-tenant scale + hardening (bead mereka-lms-72yu)
5. Deploy CMS Meilisearch config to cluster (committed, not applied)
6. Conduct load testing for library sharing at scale
7. Document library authoring workflows for course creators

## AC (Given/When/Then)
- Given Content Libraries v2 is enabled, When a course author creates a new library, Then it is stored in Blockstore and accessible via REST API
- Given a library contains OLX blocks, When a course author inserts library_content XBlock, Then content is pulled from the library into the course
- Given Meilisearch is configured, When a user searches library content, Then results are returned from indexed library blocks
- Given a library is updated, When a course references that library, Then changes propagate to all courses using that content
- Given multi-tenant mode is enabled, When a tenant creates a library, Then only that tenant can access the library content

## Verification
```bash
# Phase 1 verification (COMPLETE — commit 94e03de)
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/cms -- python manage.py cms shell -c \
  "from openedx.core.djangoapps.content_libraries.models import ContentLibrary; print(ContentLibrary.objects.filter(slug=\"platform-templates\").exists())"

# Blockstore service health
kubectl get pods -n mereka-lms -l app.kubernetes.io/name=blockstore

# Meilisearch config committed (not deployed)
git log --oneline infrastructure/tutor/plugins/mfe/patches/meilisearch-config.yml

# REST API accessibility
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $LMS_TOKEN" https://academyv2.mereka.io/api/libraries/v2/

# Library content XBlock available
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c \
  "from xmodule.library_content_block import LegacyLibraryContentBlock; print(LegacyLibraryContentBlock.__name__)"
```

## Rollback
- Phase 1 rollback: Delete platform library via Django admin or REST API
- Disable Content Libraries v2: Set waffle flag `content_libraries_v2.enabled` to False
- Remove Meilisearch config: Revert kustomize overlay changes
- Blockstore rollback: Scale deployment to 0 replicas (data preserved in persistent volume)
- No data loss — library content stored in Blockstore (persistent storage)

## Observability
- Prometheus: library_api_requests_total{endpoint,method,status}, library_content_blocks_total, blockstore_storage_bytes
- Alert: library_api_error_rate > 5% for 15m, blockstore_pod_down for 5m
- Grafana panel: Content Libraries Dashboard (library creation rate, storage usage, API latency)
- Loki: `{namespace="mereka-lms",app="cms"} |~ "content_libraries|blockstore" | logfmt`

## Security
- Library access controlled by Django permissions (staff only for platform libraries)
- Multi-tenant access enforced via organization filtering (Phase 3)
- REST API requires authentication token
- OLX content sanitized to prevent XSS in library blocks
- Audit log for library creation/modification (Django admin log)

title: Adopt bv robot protocol as standard agent workflow
description:
We have bv installed but are NOT using its graph-aware capabilities. The beads_viewer README describes a complete agent workflow we're ignoring.

## Current State (Audit)
- **bv installed**: Yes (v0.14.x)
- **Labels on beads**: ZERO. 0 out of 73 open beads have labels. This kills bv's label-health, label-flow, label-attention features entirely.
- **Acceptance Criteria in beads**: Only NEW beads (from today's session) have ACs. Old beads (P0/P1 epics like Velero DR, MongoDB, Domain Readiness) have ZERO ACs.
- **bv blurb in AGENTS.md**: Missing. Agents don't know bv exists.
- **bv --robot-triage used at session start**: Never. Agents use br ready/br list instead.
- **bv --robot-plan for parallel tracks**: Never. 62 tracks detected but unused.
- **bv --robot-suggest for hygiene**: Never. 50 suggestions sitting there (30 label, 18 missing deps, 2 dupes).
- **bv --robot-alerts**: Only 2 alerts (1 warning, 1 info) — means we're not monitoring.
- **bv --robot-insights for graph metrics**: Never. PageRank shows 1iv8=100%, 1utk=52% — we should be using this.
- **Sprint tracking**: None. No sprints configured.
- **bv --robot-priority for misalignment**: Never.

1. **Graph-theoretic triage**: PageRank, betweenness, critical path, cycles — deterministic prioritization
2. **Parallel execution tracks**: Union-Find detects 62 independent work streams
3. **Label-based domain health**: Per-label health/flow/attention analytics
4. **Hygiene automation**: Duplicate detection, missing deps, label suggestions
5. **Sprint burndown**: Progress tracking with scope change detection
6. **Priority misalignment**: Computed impact vs human priority divergence

- [ ] AC-007: Labels cover all domains: specs, infra, k8s, auth, branding, data, observability, enterprise, ci-cd

title: Mobile: Phase 2 — iOS Stabilization (PKCE, Token Lifecycle, Push, TestFlight)
description:
## Context
iOS app needs OAuth 2.0 + PKCE authentication, secure token lifecycle management, push notification integration, and a TestFlight CI/CD pipeline. Without PKCE and proper token handling, the iOS app cannot securely authenticate users or maintain sessions across app restarts and backgrounding.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC-MOB-008: OAuth 2.0 + PKCE flow via ASWebAuthenticationSession stores tokens in iOS Keychain
- [ ] AC-MOB-009: Proactive token refresh triggers <5min before expiry with single-flight (no duplicate refreshes)
- [ ] AC-MOB-010: 401 response triggers one refresh attempt; failure redirects to login (no infinite retry loop)
- [ ] AC-MOB-011: Logout revokes tokens server-side and clears Keychain
- [ ] AC-MOB-012: Push notification tap navigates to correct course/lesson content
- [ ] AC-MOB-013: GitHub Actions builds and uploads to TestFlight within 30 minutes of main branch push
- [ ] AC-MOB-014: No tokens or secrets logged to console or crash reports
- [ ] AC-MOB-015: App snapshot cleared on background (privacy protection)

## Verification
- \`scripts/qa/verify-ios-auth.sh\` (PKCE flow + token lifecycle)
- \`gh run list --repo mereka-ios --workflow=testflight.yml --limit 1\`
- Release Blocking: \`scripts/qa/verify-ios-auth.sh\`

## Outcome
- iOS app authenticates securely via PKCE with automatic token management
- Push notifications drive engagement with deep link navigation
- CI/CD delivers TestFlight builds automatically on every merge

## Negative Assertions
- [ ] AC-NEG-MOB-004: Tokens MUST NOT be logged to console, crash reports, or analytics
- [ ] AC-NEG-MOB-005: 401 retry MUST NOT loop — max 1 refresh attempt then redirect to login
- [ ] AC-NEG-MOB-006: App backgrounding MUST NOT leave sensitive data in iOS snapshot

## Evidence
- \`verify-ios-auth.sh\` output; TestFlight build number; Keychain audit (no plaintext tokens); crash report sample (no token leakage)

## Rollback
- Disable PKCE client in Django admin — users fall back to web login
- Revert TestFlight CI by disabling workflow in GitHub Actions
- Push notifications: revoke APNs certificate to stop all push delivery

## Risk
- P1 — ASWebAuthenticationSession deprecation in future iOS; mitigated by monitoring Apple WWDC announcements
- P2 — TestFlight review rejection; mitigated by following Apple Human Interface Guidelines

description:

## Context
Final mobile phase: Universal Links (iOS) and App Links (Android) for deep linking, multi-tenant branding config at launch, offline course downloads with encrypted storage, and App Store / Play Store submissions. Without deep linking, users cannot share or navigate to specific course content from external links.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC-MOB-023: Universal Link to course opens iOS app directly to that course (not Safari)
- [ ] AC-MOB-024: App Link to course opens Android app directly to that course (not Chrome)
- [ ] AC-MOB-025: Unauthenticated deep link -> login -> redirect to original content
- [ ] AC-MOB-026: org_slug=acme at app launch applies Acme branding (colors, logos) — cached with Mereka fallback
- [ ] AC-MOB-027: Offline course download stores video/HTML/PDF with encryption at rest
- [ ] AC-MOB-028: Offline quiz completion syncs to server within 60s of network restoration
- [ ] AC-MOB-029: TLS certificate pinning with 2+ intermediate CA pins (no MITM)
- [ ] AC-MOB-030: App Store and Play Store submissions accepted via phased rollout
- [ ] AC-MOB-031: No unencrypted course content stored on device filesystem

## Verification
- \`scripts/qa/verify-mobile-release.sh\`
- Manual: Tap Universal Link on iOS -> verify app opens to content
- Manual: Download course -> airplane mode -> verify playback
- Release Blocking: \`scripts/qa/verify-mobile-release.sh\` + App Store / Play Store review passes

## Outcome
- Deep links enable sharing and marketing campaigns that open directly in apps
- Multi-tenant branding delivers white-label experience per organization
- Offline mode enables learning in low-connectivity environments (rural Malaysia)
- Apps published on both stores for enterprise distribution

## Negative Assertions
- [ ] AC-NEG-MOB-010: Offline content MUST NOT be stored unencrypted on device filesystem
- [ ] AC-NEG-MOB-011: Certificate pins MUST include backup pins — single-pin failure MUST NOT brick the app
- [ ] AC-NEG-MOB-012: Offline sync MUST NOT overwrite server-side data that was updated while offline (conflict resolution required)

## Evidence
- \`verify-mobile-release.sh\` output; App Store Connect / Play Console screenshots; offline playback video recording; deep link test from SMS/email

## Rollback
- Deep links: update AASA/assetlinks.json to remove app association — links open in browser
- Offline: clear app cache — content re-downloads on next launch
- Certificate pinning: emergency app update with relaxed pins (or disable via remote config flag)

## Risk
- P1 — certificate pin rotation requires app update; mitigated by remote config kill switch for pinning
- P2 — offline sync conflicts with concurrent server changes; mitigated by last-write-wins with user notification
- P2 — App Store review rejection; mitigated by pre-review with Apple guidelines checklist

title: Assessment: Phase 3 — XQueue Grader Workers (Python + Sandbox + K8s)
description:
## Context
XQueue connects LMS to external grading services for CS/programming courses. Need Python grader workers running in a containerized sandbox with strict resource limits, deployed to K8s with auto-scaling. Without this, programming courses cannot grade code submissions automatically.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC-ASS-015: Python coding problem submission graded correctly within 30s via XQueue -> Python grader
- [ ] AC-ASS-016: Sandbox denies network access (connection refused on any outbound request)
- [ ] AC-ASS-017: Sandbox denies filesystem writes outside /tmp (permission denied)
- [ ] AC-ASS-018: Queue depth > 100 for 10 minutes triggers PagerDuty notification
- [ ] AC-ASS-019: Same submission sent twice produces identical results (idempotent grading)
- [ ] AC-ASS-020: Grader workers auto-scale 1-3 replicas based on CPU (HPA threshold 70%)
- [ ] AC-ASS-021: No secrets in grader container environment variables (ExternalSecrets only)

## Verification
- \`scripts/qa/verify-xqueue-graders.sh\`
- \`kubectl get hpa -n mereka-lms | grep xqueue\`
- \`kubectl get prometheusrule -n mereka-lms | grep xqueue\`
- Release Blocking: \`scripts/qa/verify-xqueue-graders.sh\`

## Outcome
- Python grader workers process student code submissions in sandboxed containers
- Auto-scaling handles exam-day load spikes without manual intervention
- Alerting catches queue backlog before students notice delays

## Negative Assertions
- [ ] AC-NEG-ASS-001: Grader sandbox MUST NOT allow outbound network connections (prevents code exfiltration)
- [ ] AC-NEG-ASS-002: Grader MUST NOT write outside /tmp (prevents persistent storage abuse)
- [ ] AC-NEG-ASS-003: Grader container MUST NOT run as root (securityContext.runAsNonRoot=true)

## Evidence
- \`verify-xqueue-graders.sh\` output; HPA status; PrometheusRule YAML; NetworkPolicy blocking egress

## Rollback
- \`kubectl delete deployment xqueue-grader -n mereka-lms\` — XQueue continues accepting submissions but grading pauses
- Submissions remain in queue and are processed once graders are redeployed

## Risk
- P1 — sandbox escape via Python subprocess; mitigated by seccomp + AppArmor profiles in AC-ASS-016/017
- P2 — exam-day queue spike exceeds 3 replicas; mitigated by adjusting HPA maxReplicas pre-exam

## Learning
- 1. Assessment implementation follows Open edX Django app pattern (custom-apps/ + Tutor plugin registration). 2. Always create verification script alongside implementation for regression detection.
close_reason: Phase 3 complete: XQueue grader workers with Python sandbox (seccomp+AppArmor), K8s deployment with HPA (1-3 replicas), NetworkPolicy blocking egress, PrometheusRule for queue depth alerts. 17 files, 2615 insertions. Learning: sandbox isolation requires both seccomp profiles AND NetworkPolicy — one alone is insufficient.

title: Assessment: Phase 4 — Advanced XBlocks (Drag-Drop, Math, Randomized Pools)
description:
## Context
Advanced assessment types beyond standard multiple-choice: drag-and-drop v2, math input (MathJax/LaTeX), Problem Builder, chemical equations, image annotation, and randomized question pools. Without these, the LMS cannot support STEM courses requiring interactive problem types or exam integrity via randomization.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC-ASS-022: Drag-and-drop v2 problem grades correct placement and is fully keyboard-accessible
- [ ] AC-ASS-023: Math input renders LaTeX expression and grades correctly
- [ ] AC-ASS-024: Randomized pool of 20 questions delivers 10 unique random questions per student
- [ ] AC-ASS-025: All advanced XBlocks export/import via OLX without data loss
- [ ] AC-ASS-026: All advanced XBlocks integrate with gradebook (grades recorded correctly)
- [ ] AC-ASS-027: Answer shuffling randomizes multiple-choice option order per student
- [ ] AC-ASS-028: No accessibility violations — all advanced XBlocks navigable via keyboard only

## Verification
- \`scripts/qa/verify-advanced-xblocks.sh\`
- Manual: Tab through drag-and-drop problem — verify all elements reachable
- Release Blocking: \`scripts/qa/verify-advanced-xblocks.sh\`

## Outcome
- STEM courses can use drag-and-drop, math input, and randomized pools for exams
- All advanced problem types fully accessible (WCAG 2.1 AA compliance)
- Question randomization prevents exam answer sharing between students

## Negative Assertions
- [ ] AC-NEG-ASS-004: Randomized pool MUST NOT serve the same question set to two students in the same exam session
- [ ] AC-NEG-ASS-005: OLX export of advanced XBlocks MUST NOT lose interactive element configuration
- [ ] AC-NEG-ASS-006: Math input MUST NOT accept arbitrary script tags (XSS prevention)

## Evidence

## Rollback
