title: Badges: Deploy Credentials + Badges System (32 ACs)
description:
## Context
Badges epic — deploy Credentials service and Open Badges 2.0 system. Credentials service is deployed (health check passing, badges migrations run) but no badge classes are configured, no issuer exists, and no certificates are being generated. Without this, students receive no verifiable credentials for course completion. Spec: specs/badges-credentials-enterprise_spec.md (Tier 7, 32 ACs).

## Outcome
- Badge Issuer configured in Credentials service (Open Badges 2.0)
- Badge Classes created for course completion, program completion, achievement milestones
- Certificate generation pipeline: course completion → credential issued → badge awarded
- Badge assertion verification endpoint public and functional
- Credentials service fully themed with Mereka Academy branding
- Backpack integration for badge portability (Mozilla Backpack / Credly)
- 32/32 spec ACs verified green

## Non-goals
- Custom badge design tool (pre-designed badges only)
- Blockchain-verified credentials
- Badge revocation workflow (issue-only in MVP)
- Enterprise-specific badge classes (shared classes only)

## Constraints
- Credentials service already deployed at port 8150
- Open Badges 2.0 specification compliance required
- Badge images must be SVG/PNG and hosted on CDN
- Issuer URL must be publicly accessible for verification

## Plan
1. Create Badge Issuer in Credentials admin (Mereka Academy)
2. Design badge images (SVG format, brand-compliant)
3. Create Badge Classes: course completion, program completion, milestone
4. Configure certificate generation pipeline in LMS
5. Test end-to-end: complete course → certificate → badge
6. Set up public badge assertion verification endpoint
7. Test Backpack integration (export badge to external service)
8. Complete branding for Credentials service

## AC (Given/When/Then)
- Given a Badge Issuer exists, When a student completes a course, Then a badge assertion is created in Credentials service
- Given a badge is issued, When the verification URL is accessed publicly, Then the badge assertion JSON validates against Open Badges 2.0
- Given a student has earned badges, When they visit their Credentials dashboard, Then all earned badges are displayed with download options
- Given Backpack integration is configured, When a student exports a badge, Then it appears in their external Backpack
- Given the Credentials service is themed, When a student views their certificate, Then Mereka Academy branding is displayed

## Verification
```bash
# Credentials service health
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/credentials -- curl -sf http://localhost:8150/health/ -H "Host: credentials.academyv2.mereka.io"

# Badge Issuer exists
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/credentials -- python manage.py shell -c \
  "from credentials.apps.badges.models import BadgeIssuer; print(BadgeIssuer.objects.count())"

# Badge Classes exist
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/credentials -- python manage.py shell -c \
  "from credentials.apps.badges.models import BadgeClass; print(BadgeClass.objects.count())"

# Badges table has data
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/credentials -- python manage.py shell -c \
  "from credentials.apps.badges.models import BadgeAssertion; print(BadgeAssertion.objects.count())"
```

## Rollback
- Disable certificate generation: set ENABLE_CERTIFICATES=False in LMS
- Credentials service remains running but stops issuing new badges
- Existing badges preserved in database
- Badge assertion URLs remain accessible (public verification)

## Observability
- Prometheus: badges_issued_total{badge_class}, certificate_generation_duration_seconds
- Alert: certificate_generation_failure_rate > 5%
- Grafana panel in Credentials Operations dashboard
- Loki: `{app="credentials"} |~ "badge|certificate" | logfmt`

## Security
- Badge assertion URLs are public but tamper-proof (signed)
- Credentials admin requires staff permission
- Badge images hosted on CDN with integrity hash
- No PII in public badge assertions (only user display name)

## Docs
- docs/operations/CREDENTIALS_RUNBOOK.md (to create)
- specs/badges-credentials-enterprise_spec.md (source of truth)

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: Credentials service deployment (DONE), badge image design (EXTERNAL)
- Blocks: nothing (terminal epic)

## Owner
gurpreet (platform lead) — requires badge image design

title: Tenancy: Phase 3 — Operational Hardening (Offboarding + Scale Testing)
description:
## Context
With 2 tenants validated (Phase 2), the platform needs operational hardening for production: tenant offboarding with data export, nightly isolation regression tests, and load testing at 10-tenant scale. Without this, there is no safe way to remove a tenant or detect isolation regressions before they become security incidents.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC-TEN-014: offboard-tenant.sh exports data, deactivates tenant, enforces 30-day grace period, then deletes all records with immutable audit trail
- [ ] AC-TEN-015: After offboarding completes, zero enterprise_catalog records exist for the offboarded tenant UUID
- [ ] AC-TEN-016: After offboarding completes, zero ClickHouse events exist for the offboarded tenant UUID
- [ ] AC-TEN-017: Nightly K8s CronJob runs isolation tests and fires Critical alert within 5 minutes of any cross-tenant leakage
- [ ] AC-TEN-018: Enterprise catalog API p95 latency <= 300ms with 10 active tenants
- [ ] AC-TEN-019: No tenant p95 exceeds 120% of single-tenant baseline
- [ ] AC-TEN-020: Offboarding audit log entry contains action, tenant UUID, actor, and timestamp
- [ ] AC-TEN-021: No data deletion occurs before 30-day grace period expires (PDPA/GDPR compliance)

## Verification
- `scripts/tenants/offboard-tenant.sh --slug test-tenant --dry-run`
- `scripts/qa/verify-tenant-hardening.sh`
- `kubectl get cronjob -n mereka-lms | grep tenant-isolation`
- `scripts/qa/load-test-tenants.sh --count 10`
- Release Blocking: `scripts/qa/verify-tenant-hardening.sh`

## Outcome
- Offboarding pipeline safely removes tenants with full data export and audit trail
- Nightly CronJob detects cross-tenant leakage before any user sees it
- Platform proven stable at 10-tenant scale (p95 < 300ms)

## Negative Assertions
- [ ] AC-NEG-TEN-001: Offboarding MUST NOT delete any data before 30-day grace period expires
- [ ] AC-NEG-TEN-002: Nightly isolation test MUST NOT access production tenant data (synthetic only)
- [ ] AC-NEG-TEN-003: Load test MUST NOT run against production cluster without explicit --production flag

## Evidence
- `scripts/tenants/offboard-tenant.sh --dry-run` output; CronJob YAML in deploy/k8s/; load test results in docs/operations/

## Rollback
- Delete CronJob: `kubectl delete cronjob tenant-isolation-test -n mereka-lms`
- Revert offboarding: data export is non-destructive; grace period prevents premature deletion
- Load test is read-only synthetic — no rollback needed

## Risk
- P1 — offboarding data export may exceed 5-day window for large tenants; mitigated by streaming export in AC-TEN-014
- P2 — nightly CronJob false positives; mitigated by threshold tuning in AC-TEN-017

## Learning
- 1. Tenancy implementation follows Open edX Django app pattern (custom-apps/ + Tutor plugin registration). 2. Always create verification script alongside implementation for regression detection.
close_reason: Phase 3 complete: offboard_tenant.py management command with 30-day grace period + audit trail, nightly CronJob for isolation regression tests, PrometheusRule alerts (TenantIsolationFailure, TenantIsolationTestMissing), load-test-tenants.sh for synthetic 10-tenant scale test. 7 files, 1303 insertions. Learning: offboarding requires a grace period AND audit trail — grace period alone doesn't satisfy PDPA/GDPR.

title: Email: Phase 5 — Templates + Bulk Campaigns
description:
## Context
Email Phase 5 — multi-language templates and bulk campaigns. Currently no email templates exist beyond Django defaults, and there is no campaign engine for bulk emails. Without this, all emails are plain text with no branding, and marketing/announcement emails require manual sending. Plan: specs/plans/email-notifications-pipeline_plan.md Phase 5.

## Outcome
- 15 ACE message type templates covering: welcome, enrollment, grade, certificate, deadline, forum, password reset, account activation, course announcement, survey, marketing promo, re-engagement, feedback, maintenance notice, campaign
- Each template available in EN, MS, ZH-Hans (45 template files total)
- Per-tenant branding injection (logo, colors, footer) via TenantConfig
- Bulk campaign engine: schedule, pause/resume, segmentation (by course, cohort, enrollment date)
- Per-tenant rate limiting (50 emails/sec per tenant)
- Content sanitization (no XSS in HTML templates)
- Template preview API for campaign authors

## Non-goals
- Drag-and-drop email builder (code-based templates only)
- A/B testing of email content
- Third-party email marketing integration (Mailchimp, SendGrid)
- SMS campaigns

## Constraints
- SES sending rate must respect per-tenant limits (50/sec)
- Templates must use Django template language (not Jinja2)
- ZH-Hans translations require professional translation (EXTERNAL)
- Campaign scheduling must handle timezone differences per user

## Plan
1. Create 15 ACE message type template files (EN base)
2. Add MS translations for all 15 templates
3. Add ZH-Hans translations for all 15 templates
4. Implement per-tenant branding injection in template context
5. Build campaign engine: create, schedule, pause/resume
6. Add segmentation: by course, cohort, enrollment date
7. Implement per-tenant rate limiting (token bucket, 50/sec)
8. Add content sanitization to template rendering
9. Build template preview API

## AC (Given/When/Then)
- Given a student's language preference is MS, When a welcome email is sent, Then the Malay template is used
- Given a tenant has custom branding, When any email is sent to their users, Then the email includes tenant's logo and colors
- Given a campaign is scheduled for 14:00 UTC, When the scheduler runs, Then the campaign starts sending at 14:00 UTC
- Given a campaign is paused, When the pause API is called, Then sending stops within 30 seconds
- Given per-tenant rate is 50/sec, When 100 emails are queued, Then they send over 2 seconds (not burst)
- Given a template contains <script> tags, When the sanitizer runs, Then the tags are stripped

## Verification
```bash
# Template files exist
ls infrastructure/tutor/templates/email/ | wc -l  # Should be >= 45

# Campaign engine
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c \
  "from openedx.core.djangoapps.email_campaigns.models import Campaign; print(Campaign.objects.count())"

# Rate limiting
# Send 100 test emails, verify they take >= 2 seconds
```

title: Email: Phase 3 — In-App Notifications
description:
## Context
Email Phase 3 — in-app notifications. Currently LMS has no in-app notification center. Users miss important events (enrollment confirmations, grade updates, forum replies) when they are not checking email. Without this, engagement suffers and users lack awareness of platform activity. Plan: specs/plans/email-notifications-pipeline_plan.md Phase 3.

## Outcome
- Notification store MySQL model with UUID primary key and cursor pagination
- REST API: GET /notifications/ (list), PATCH /notifications/<id>/read, POST /notifications/mark-all-read, GET /notifications/unread-count, DELETE /notifications/<id>/
- ACE in_app channel delivering to notification store
- Signal handlers for: enrollment, grade update, certificate awarded, forum reply
- Flood batching: collapse 10+ same-type events into summary notification
- 90-day automatic purge via management command + CronJob

## Non-goals
- Real-time WebSocket push (polling-based in MVP)
- Notification preferences UI in mobile app (web only)
- Rich media notifications (text only in MVP)
- Cross-device sync of read status

## Constraints
- MySQL notification table — not a separate service
- Cursor pagination required (not offset-based) for performance at scale
- Flood batching must be configurable per notification type
- 90-day purge must run off-peak hours

## Plan
1. Create Notification model (UUID pk, user, type, message, read, created_at)
2. Build REST API with DRF serializers
3. Implement ACE in_app channel
4. Wire signal handlers for enrollment/grade/certificate/forum events
5. Add flood batching logic (collapse threshold: 10)
6. Create purge management command + CronJob (90 days)
7. Add unread count to LMS header component

## AC (Given/When/Then)
- Given a student enrolls in a course, When the enrollment signal fires, Then a notification appears in their notification list via API
- Given a student has 15 unread notifications, When they call GET /notifications/unread-count, Then the response shows 15
- Given 12 forum reply notifications arrive within 1 minute, When flood batching runs, Then they collapse into 1 summary notification
- Given a notification is 91 days old, When the purge CronJob runs, Then it is deleted from the database
- Given a student reads a notification, When they PATCH /notifications/<id>/read, Then the unread count decrements by 1

## Verification
```bash
# Notification API
curl -sf -H "Authorization: JWT $TOKEN" https://academyv2.mereka.io/api/notifications/unread-count

# Notification model
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c \
  "from openedx.core.djangoapps.notifications.models import Notification; print(Notification.objects.count())"

# CronJob
kubectl get cronjob -n mereka-lms | grep notification-purge
```

## Rollback
- Disable ACE in_app channel: remove from INSTALLED_APPS
- API remains but returns empty results
- Notification table preserved (can re-enable later)
- Signal handlers: disconnect via Django signal disconnect

## Observability
- Prometheus: notifications_created_total{type}, notifications_read_total, notifications_purged_total
- Alert: notification_delivery_latency > 30s
- Grafana panel in Notification Pipeline dashboard
- Loki: `{app="lms"} |~ "notification" | logfmt`

## Security
- API requires JWT authentication
- Users can only see their own notifications (user_id filter enforced at ORM level)
- Notification content sanitized (no HTML injection)
- Purge job runs with least-privilege ServiceAccount

## Docs
- docs/architecture/NOTIFICATION_PIPELINE.md (add in-app section)
- specs/email-notifications-pipeline_spec.md Phase 3 ACs

title: Libraries: Phase 3-4 — Multi-Tenant Scale + Hardening
description:
## Context
After single-tenant library validation (Phase 2), Content Libraries v2 must scale to all tenants with usage tracking via xAPI, analytics dashboards, load testing at 100/500 library scale, and security hardening. Without this, libraries work for one tenant but degrade or leak data under multi-tenant production load.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC-LIB-026: New tenant provisioned via provision-tenant.sh can create libraries immediately
- [ ] AC-LIB-027: library_content_viewed xAPI event appears in ClickHouse when library content is viewed
- [ ] AC-LIB-028: Search returns results in <1s with 100 libraries / 5K components
- [ ] AC-LIB-029: Page loads in <2s with 500 libraries / 50K components
- [ ] AC-LIB-030: Nightly backup CronJob exports all library content to backup storage without errors
- [ ] AC-LIB-031: OWASP Top 10 security review passes for user-authored library content (XSS, injection)
- [ ] AC-LIB-032: No cross-tenant library access in any code path (security audit verified)

## Verification
- \`scripts/qa/load-test-libraries.sh --libraries=100 --components=5000\`
- \`scripts/qa/load-test-libraries.sh --libraries=500 --components=50000\`
- \`kubectl get cronjob -n mereka-lms | grep library-backup\`
- \`kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/clickhouse -- clickhouse-client -q "SELECT count() FROM xapi_events WHERE verb_id LIKE '%library%'"\`
- Release Blocking: \`scripts/qa/load-test-libraries.sh --libraries=500 --components=50000\`

## Outcome
- Libraries production-ready at multi-tenant scale with xAPI analytics
- Security hardened against XSS/injection in user-authored content
- Nightly backups ensure disaster recovery capability

## Negative Assertions
- [ ] AC-NEG-LIB-013: xAPI events MUST NOT contain PII beyond user ID (no email, name, IP in event payload)
- [ ] AC-NEG-LIB-014: User-authored library content MUST NOT execute JavaScript (XSS sanitization enforced)
- [ ] AC-NEG-LIB-015: Load test MUST NOT be runnable against production without explicit --production flag

## Evidence
- Load test latency reports at 100/500 scale; ClickHouse xAPI event sample; OWASP security audit report; cross-tenant penetration test results

## Rollback
- xAPI events: disable library_content_viewed signal handler
- Backup CronJob: \`kubectl delete cronjob library-backup -n mereka-lms\`
- Security: content sanitization is defense-in-depth — disabling one layer doesn't create vulnerability

## Risk
- P1 — xAPI event volume overwhelms ClickHouse at scale; mitigated by batch insert with buffering
- P1 — user-authored content XSS bypass; mitigated by server-side sanitization + CSP headers in AC-LIB-031
- P2 — backup storage costs at multi-tenant scale; mitigated by per-tenant retention policies

- Add a runbook for rotating MySQL users to match the canonical secret values without downtime.

Acceptance:

- Services can restart without DB auth regressions.
- CI/ops check flags newline drift early.

title: Email: Phase 2 — Preferences Service (GDPR consent)
description:
## Context
Email Phase 2 — user preferences and GDPR consent. Without this, users cannot control which emails they receive, violating GDPR Article 7 (consent) and Article 21 (right to object). Currently all LMS emails are sent unconditionally. Plan: specs/plans/email-notifications-pipeline_plan.md Phase 2.

## Outcome
- Preferences REST API deployed at /api/user/v1/preferences/email/ with rate limiting (60 req/min)
- GDPR consent tracking: explicit opt-in recorded with timestamp and consent version
- One-click unsubscribe via HMAC-signed URL (RFC 8058 compliant)
- List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post headers in all marketing emails
- Preferences enforcement in ACE dispatch: emails blocked if user has opted out of category
- Admin API to view/export consent records for GDPR SAR requests

## Non-goals
- In-app notification preferences (Phase 3)
- Push notification preferences (Phase 4)
- Email template customization (Phase 5)
- Per-course email preferences (too granular for MVP)

## Constraints
- Must comply with GDPR Article 7 (consent) and Article 21 (right to object)
- HMAC unsubscribe URLs must not expire (permanent opt-out)
- Preferences API must handle concurrent updates (optimistic locking)
- Must work with existing ACE (Automated Communication Engine) dispatch pipeline

## Plan
1. Create email_preferences Django model (user, category, opted_in, consent_version, timestamp)
2. Build REST API: GET/PUT /api/user/v1/preferences/email/
3. Add rate limiting to preferences API (60 req/min per user)
4. Implement GDPR consent tracking (opt-in with version, audit trail)
5. Generate HMAC-signed one-click unsubscribe URLs
6. Add List-Unsubscribe headers to ACE email templates
7. Wire preferences check into ACE dispatch (pre-send filter)
8. Build admin API for consent record export (GDPR SAR)
9. Add Prometheus metrics: email_preferences_changes_total, email_unsubscribe_total

## AC (Given/When/Then)
- Given a user is authenticated, When they GET /api/user/v1/preferences/email/, Then they receive their current email preferences by category
- Given a user opts out of "marketing" emails, When LMS sends a marketing email, Then the email is blocked by ACE dispatch and a metric is incremented
- Given a marketing email is sent, When the recipient clicks the one-click unsubscribe link, Then they are immediately opted out without login required
- Given GDPR SAR request, When admin calls /api/admin/consent-records/?user=<id>, Then all consent records for that user are returned with timestamps
- Given >60 requests/min to preferences API, When the 61st request arrives, Then HTTP 429 is returned

## Verification
```bash
# Preferences API
curl -sf -H "Authorization: JWT $TOKEN" https://academyv2.mereka.io/api/user/v1/preferences/email/

# HMAC unsubscribe
# Generate test URL, verify it returns 200 and updates preferences
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c \
  "from openedx.core.djangoapps.email_preferences.utils import generate_unsubscribe_url; print(generate_unsubscribe_url(1, 'marketing'))"

# ACE dispatch filter
kubectl logs -n mereka-lms deploy/lms --tail=100 | grep "email_preference_blocked"

# Consent records
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c \
  "from openedx.core.djangoapps.email_preferences.models import ConsentRecord; print(ConsentRecord.objects.count())"
```

## Rollback
- Disable ACE dispatch filter: set ENABLE_EMAIL_PREFERENCES=False in LMS settings
- API remains available but becomes no-op
- Existing consent records preserved in database
- Remove List-Unsubscribe headers from ACE templates

## Observability
- Prometheus: email_preferences_changes_total{category}, email_unsubscribe_total{method="one_click|api"}
- Alert: email_unsubscribe_rate > 5% of total sends (indicates quality problem)
- Grafana panel in Email Operations dashboard
- Loki: `{app="lms"} |~ "email_preference" | logfmt`

## Security
- HMAC-signed unsubscribe URLs (SHA-256, server-side secret)
- Preferences API requires JWT authentication
- Consent records immutable (append-only, no deletion)
- Admin consent export requires staff permission + audit log entry

## Docs
- docs/operations/EMAIL_INFRASTRUCTURE.md (add preferences section)
- docs/architecture/GDPR_COMPLIANCE.md (to create)
- specs/email-notifications-pipeline_spec.md Phase 2 ACs

title: Fix ArgoCD ConfigMap churn causing LMS pod rolling every 3-5 min
description:
The LMS deployment rolls (new pods every 3-5 min) due to CSS ConfigMap hash changes in Git.

Root cause: ConfigMaps openedx-overrides-runtime-css and openedx-theme-head-extra-patched change hash suffixes between commits. ArgoCD selfHeal=true detects drift and triggers rolling update.

Impact:
- Pod instability (any long-running kubectl exec gets killed)
- Wasted resources (constant pod cycling)
- Made Kajabi import much harder (needed resilient import script)

Fix options:
1. Stop committing CSS changes so frequently
2. Add ignoreDifferences in ArgoCD Application for those ConfigMaps
3. Consolidate CSS into a stable ConfigMap
4. Use Kustomize configMapGenerator with consistent naming

Evidence: 9 replica sets in 45 minutes observed during Kajabi import (2026-02-09).
close_reason: ArgoCD ignoreDifferences patch created at deploy/k8s/patches/argocd-configmap-ignore.yaml. Apply with kubectl patch.

title: SSO/OAuth for Kajabi-migrated users (April 2026)
description:
## Context
Kajabi-migrated users need seamless SSO login to the LMS. These users currently have basic accounts but no SSO integration. Without this, migrated users must manage separate credentials, increasing support burden and reducing adoption. Target: April 2026.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC-SSO-001: OAuth2 client registered (mereka-kajabi-sso) and Kajabi user with email user@example.com matched to existing LMS account via SSO
- [ ] AC-SSO-002: Bulk import of 500-user CSV creates/links 500 accounts with zero duplicates
- [ ] AC-SSO-003: SSO failure falls back to email/password login (no lockout)
- [ ] AC-SSO-004: No duplicate accounts created during migration (email + username deduplication enforced)
- [ ] AC-SSO-005: Welcome email sent to each migrated user with SSO setup instructions

## Verification
- \`scripts/qa/verify-kajabi-sso.sh\`
- \`kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c "from django.contrib.auth.models import User; print(User.objects.count())"\`
- Release Blocking: \`scripts/qa/verify-kajabi-sso.sh\`

## Outcome
- Kajabi users log in via SSO with zero credential management overhead
- Bulk import handles 500+ users with deduplication guarantees
- Graceful fallback prevents user lockout during SSO issues

## Negative Assertions
- [ ] AC-NEG-SSO-001: Bulk import MUST NOT create duplicate accounts for existing email addresses
- [ ] AC-NEG-SSO-002: SSO failure MUST NOT prevent email/password login (fallback mandatory)
- [ ] AC-NEG-SSO-003: Welcome emails MUST NOT be sent to already-active SSO users (only new migrations)

## Evidence
- OAuth2 client registration in Django admin; bulk import log with dedup stats; SSO login screenshot; fallback login test

## Rollback
- Disable SSO backend in \`AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS\` — users fall back to email/password
- Bulk import is additive — no data destroyed; roll back by deactivating linked accounts

## Risk
- P1 — email deduplication fails on case-sensitive matching; mitigated by lowercase normalization in AC-SSO-004
- P2 — welcome email delivery issues (spam filtering); mitigated by SPF/DKIM on sending domain

## Migration Execution: DEFERRED

> **DO NOT execute bulk Kajabi user import until further notice from gurpreet.** The SSO/OAuth app code (openedx_kajabi_sso) is ready and merged, but the actual migration (running import_kajabi_users management command) is deferred. Previous migrations have already been done — this is not a first-time setup. Wait for explicit go-ahead before importing any users.

title: Proctoring: Integrate Enterprise Proctoring (38 ACs)
description:
## Context
Proctoring epic — integrate enterprise proctoring for high-stakes assessments. No proctoring capability exists. Enterprise clients requiring proctored exams (certification, compliance training) cannot be served. This is the lowest-priority epic (Tier 8) but critical for enterprise B2B contracts. Spec: specs/proctoring-integration_spec.md (Tier 8, 38 ACs). Plan: specs/plans/proctoring-integration_plan.md.

## Outcome
- Proctoring provider integrated (Examity or ProctorU via edx-proctoring)
- Exam session lifecycle: create → start → monitor → end → review
- Proctoring dashboard for instructors (review flagged sessions)
- Enterprise-scoped proctoring settings (per-tenant provider config)
- Proctoring backend configured in LMS settings (edx-proctoring Django app)
- 38/38 spec ACs verified green

## Non-goals
- Custom proctoring AI (use provider's AI monitoring)
- Browser lockdown (rely on provider's browser extension)
- Offline proctoring
- Multiple simultaneous proctoring providers per tenant

## Constraints
- Proctoring provider contract required (EXTERNAL — enterprise sales)
- edx-proctoring Django app must be compatible with current edx-platform
- Exam scheduling must integrate with course schedule
- Provider API credentials per enterprise tenant

## Plan
1. Select proctoring provider (Examity or ProctorU)
2. Sign provider contract and get API credentials
3. Configure edx-proctoring Django app in LMS
4. Register provider backend in LMS settings
5. Create test proctored exam in sample course
6. Test exam session lifecycle end-to-end
7. Build instructor proctoring dashboard
8. Configure per-tenant proctoring settings
9. Run pilot with enterprise client

## AC (Given/When/Then)
- Given a proctored exam is configured, When a student starts the exam, Then the proctoring provider's session begins
- Given the student completes the exam, When the session ends, Then the recording is submitted for review
- Given the provider flags suspicious behavior, When the instructor opens the dashboard, Then they see the flagged session with review options
- Given per-tenant proctoring is configured, When tenant A's exam starts, Then it uses tenant A's provider settings
- Given a student has no webcam, When they try to start a proctored exam, Then they see a clear error about requirements

## Verification
```bash
# edx-proctoring installed
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c \
  "import edx_proctoring; print(edx_proctoring.__version__)"

# Proctoring backend configured
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c \
  "from django.conf import settings; print(settings.PROCTORING_BACKENDS)"

# Full verification
./scripts/qa/verify-proctoring.sh
```

## Rollback
- Disable proctoring: remove backend from PROCTORING_BACKENDS setting
- Existing proctored exams revert to unproctored mode
- Provider API credentials: revoke in provider's admin panel
- Student exam data preserved (grade history unaffected)

## Observability
- Prometheus: proctoring_sessions_total{status="started|completed|flagged|error"}
- Alert: proctoring_session_error_rate > 5%
- Grafana dashboard: Proctoring Operations
- Loki: `{app="lms"} |~ "proctoring" | logfmt`

## Security
- Provider API credentials via ExternalSecrets
- Proctoring recordings handled by provider (not stored locally)
- Student consent required before proctoring session starts
- FERPA/GDPR compliance for recording data
- Exam content not transmitted to proctoring provider

## Docs
- docs/operations/PROCTORING_RUNBOOK.md (to create)
- specs/proctoring-integration_spec.md (source of truth)

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: Proctoring provider contract (EXTERNAL — enterprise sales)
- Blocks: nothing (terminal epic)
- Related: mereka-lms-1si5 (Assessment epic)

## Owner
gurpreet (platform lead) — requires enterprise sales coordination

title: Mobile: Deploy Enterprise Mobile Apps (37 ACs)
description:
## Context
Mobile apps epic — deploy enterprise-grade iOS and Android apps for Mereka Academy. Currently no mobile apps exist. Students access the LMS via mobile browser only, which lacks push notifications, offline access, and native UX. Spec: specs/mobile-apps-enterprise_spec.md (Tier 7, 37 ACs). Plan: specs/plans/mobile-apps-enterprise_plan.md.

## Outcome
- iOS app published to TestFlight (pre-release) and App Store
- Android app published to Google Play (internal track and production)
- OAuth2 authentication flow working end-to-end (authorization code + PKCE)
- Course browsing, enrollment, and content consumption functional
- Push notifications via FCM (linked to email Phase 4)
- Firebase Analytics and Crashlytics integrated
- 37/37 spec ACs verified green

## Non-goals
- Offline course content download (future release)
- In-app purchases or subscriptions
- Custom mobile-specific features beyond Open edX mobile SDK
- Tablet-optimized layouts (phone-first)

## Constraints
- iOS requires Apple Developer Account ($99/year) and Xcode on macOS
- Android requires Google Play Developer Account ($25 one-time)
- OAuth2 redirect URI scheme must be registered in LMS
- Mobile app secrets managed via Infisical → GCP SM → CI/CD (docs/operations/MOBILE_SECRETS_MANAGEMENT.md)

## Plan
1. Set up iOS project (Xcode, provisioning profiles, signing)
2. Set up Android project (Android Studio, keystore, signing)
3. Configure OAuth2 application in LMS for mobile apps
4. Build and deploy to TestFlight / Play Store internal track
5. Integrate Firebase Analytics and Crashlytics
6. Integrate push notifications (FCM)
7. QA: test on 3+ iOS devices, 3+ Android devices
8. Submit to App Store / Play Store production

## AC (Given/When/Then)
- Given the iOS app is installed, When a user taps login, Then the OAuth2 flow opens a web view to the LMS login page
- Given valid credentials, When the user completes login, Then they are returned to the app with a valid access token
- Given a user is logged in, When they browse courses, Then all enrolled courses are visible
- Given push notifications are enabled, When a course announcement is published, Then the student receives a push notification
- Given Crashlytics is integrated, When the app crashes, Then the crash report appears in Firebase Console

## Verification
```bash
# OAuth2 app exists
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c \
  "from oauth2_provider.models import Application; print(Application.objects.filter(name__contains='mobile').count())"

# Mobile secrets in GCP SM
gcloud secrets list --filter="name~MEREKA_LMS_MOBILE_" --format="table(name)" --project bbi-k8

# Verify mobile secrets inventory
./scripts/qa/verify-mobile-secrets-inventory.sh
```

## Rollback
- Remove app from TestFlight / Play Store
- Revoke OAuth2 application in LMS admin
- Firebase project: disable app in Firebase Console
- User data in app: cleared on uninstall

## Observability
- Firebase Analytics: DAU, session duration, screen views
- Crashlytics: crash-free rate, top crash reports
- Prometheus: oauth2_mobile_token_grant_total{platform}
- Alert: mobile_crash_free_rate < 99% (Firebase)

## Security
- OAuth2 with PKCE (no client secret stored on device)
- Tokens stored in iOS Keychain / Android EncryptedSharedPreferences
- Certificate pinning for API calls
- Mobile secrets quarterly rotation (docs/operations/MOBILE_SECRETS_MANAGEMENT.md)

title: Email: Phase 4 — Push Notifications (FCM)
description:
## Context
Email Phase 4 — push notifications via FCM. Mobile users miss notifications when not actively using the web app. Without push, the mobile experience feels disconnected. Requires Firebase project setup and mobile app integration. Plan: specs/plans/email-notifications-pipeline_plan.md Phase 4.

## Outcome
- ACE push channel integrated with FCM HTTP v1 API
- FCM batch sending (up to 500 per request)
- Device registration model + REST API for iOS/Android token management
- org_slug isolation (notifications scoped to tenant)
- iOS/Android notification grouping (collapse similar notifications)
- Notification delivery confirmation tracking

## Non-goals
- Web push notifications (browser notifications)
- Rich media push (images, video thumbnails)
- Notification scheduling (send immediately only)
- Push notification analytics beyond delivery rate

## Constraints
- Firebase project must be created and configured (EXTERNAL dependency)
- FCM HTTP v1 API requires OAuth2 service account credentials
- iOS requires APNs certificate + FCM bridge
- org_slug isolation must prevent cross-tenant notification leakage

## Plan
1. Create Firebase project for Mereka Academy
2. Generate FCM service account key
3. Store key in Infisical → GCP SM → ExternalSecrets
4. Create DeviceRegistration model (user, platform, token, org_slug)
5. Build device registration REST API
6. Implement ACE push channel using FCM HTTP v1
7. Add batch sending (500 per request)
8. Implement notification grouping per platform
9. Add org_slug isolation to push dispatch

## AC (Given/When/Then)
- Given a mobile user registers their device, When they POST /api/devices/register, Then their FCM token is stored with org_slug
- Given a notification event fires for a mobile user, When ACE push channel dispatches, Then an FCM push notification is delivered to their device
- Given 600 devices need notification, When batch sending executes, Then 2 FCM API calls are made (500 + 100)
- Given tenant A user is registered, When a tenant B notification fires, Then the tenant A user does NOT receive it
- Given a user has 5 rapid notifications, When iOS grouping applies, Then they see a single grouped notification

## Verification
```bash
# Device registration
curl -sf -H "Authorization: JWT $TOKEN" https://academyv2.mereka.io/api/devices/ | jq '.count'

# FCM test send
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c \
  "from openedx.core.djangoapps.push_notifications.tasks import send_test_push; send_test_push('<device_token>')"

# org_slug isolation
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c \
  "from openedx.core.djangoapps.push_notifications.models import DeviceRegistration; print(DeviceRegistration.objects.values('org_slug').distinct())"
```

## Rollback
- Disable ACE push channel: remove from NOTIFICATION_CHANNELS config
- Device registrations preserved (no data loss)
- FCM credentials: revoke in Firebase Console
- Existing email/in-app notifications unaffected

## Observability
- Prometheus: fcm_push_sent_total{platform,status}, fcm_push_latency_seconds
- Alert: fcm_push_failure_rate > 5% for 30m
- Grafana panel in Notification Pipeline dashboard
- Loki: `{app="lms"} |~ "fcm_push" | logfmt`

## Security
- FCM service account key via ExternalSecrets (never in code)
- Device tokens are sensitive — encrypted at rest in MySQL
- org_slug isolation enforced at dispatch level (not just API level)
- Rate limiting on device registration API (prevent token stuffing)

## Docs
- docs/architecture/NOTIFICATION_PIPELINE.md (add push section)
- specs/email-notifications-pipeline_spec.md Phase 4 ACs
- Mobile app setup: docs/MOBILE_IOS_APP_SETUP.md

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: Phase 3 in-app notifications (mereka-lms-4uz3), Firebase project setup (EXTERNAL)
- Blocks: Phase 5 templates + campaigns (mereka-lms-4le9)
- Parent: mereka-lms-2t3y (Email epic)
- Related: mereka-lms-mci9 (Mobile epic)

gurpreet (platform lead) — requires Firebase project creation

## Learning
- 1. Email implementation follows Open edX Django app pattern (custom-apps/ + Tutor plugin registration). 2. Always create verification script alongside implementation for regression detection.

title: Libraries: Phase 1 — Platform Libraries (Lifecycle, Components, Versioning, Reuse)
description:
## Context
Core library functionality: CRUD operations, component authoring, draft/published versioning, and cross-course reuse via library_content XBlock. Without this, course authors cannot create reusable content components and must duplicate content manually across courses.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC-LIB-007: Library with 50 components publishes atomically — all components available in courses within 30s
- [ ] AC-LIB-008: library_content XBlock configured for 5 random from 20 renders 5 unique components per student load
- [ ] AC-LIB-009: Soft-deleted library restores with all components and version history intact
- [ ] AC-LIB-010: library_v2_ref XBlock shows "update available" notification in Studio when source library component changes
- [ ] AC-LIB-011: First platform library lib:Mereka:platform-templates created and usable
- [ ] AC-LIB-012: Rollback to any previous library version restores exact prior state
- [ ] AC-LIB-013: No orphaned Blockstore data after library deletion (reference tracking accurate)

## Verification
- \`scripts/qa/verify-libraries-core.sh\`
- \`kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/cms -- python manage.py cms shell -c "from openedx.core.djangoapps.content_libraries.api import get_libraries; print(len(list(get_libraries())))"\`
- Release Blocking: \`scripts/qa/verify-libraries-core.sh\`

## Outcome
- Course authors create reusable content libraries with draft/published workflow
- Cross-course reuse eliminates manual content duplication
- Version control enables safe rollback to any prior library state

## Negative Assertions
- [ ] AC-NEG-LIB-004: Library publish MUST NOT partially apply — all-or-nothing atomic publish
- [ ] AC-NEG-LIB-005: Soft-deleted library MUST NOT be permanently deleted before 30-day retention period
- [ ] AC-NEG-LIB-006: library_content randomization MUST NOT serve the same set to the same student on reload

## Evidence
- \`verify-libraries-core.sh\` output; lib:Mereka:platform-templates visible in Studio; version history showing rollback capability

## Rollback
- Disable CONTENT_LIBRARIES_V2_ENABLED feature flag — courses fall back to v1 libraries
- Individual library deletion: \`python manage.py cms delete_library <lib_key>\`
- Blockstore data cleanup: garbage collection script for orphaned references

## Risk
- P1 — atomic publish fails mid-operation leaving partial state; mitigated by database transaction wrapping in AC-LIB-007
- P2 — Blockstore storage growth with version history; mitigated by configurable retention policy

title: Tenancy: Phase 0 — Foundation (Model + Cache + Feature Flags)
description:
## Context
Foundation layer for multi-tenant architecture. Without this, no tenant isolation exists — all users share a single context. This phase establishes the data model linking, cache namespacing, analytics tagging, and feature flags needed before provisioning any tenant.

## Outcome
- EnterpriseCustomer ↔ Django Site mapping via site_id FK configured
- Redis cache keys namespaced by tenant UUID (format: enterprise:{uuid}:{key_type}:{key_id})
- ClickHouse xAPI events table has enterprise_customer_uuid column (nullable)
- xAPI event producer tags events with enterprise_customer_uuid
- Feature flags created: ENABLE_MULTI_TENANT_BRANDING, ENABLE_TENANT_ANALYTICS_SCOPING
- Tenant branding directory structure created: infrastructure/tutor/themes/mereka/tenants/
- SiteConfiguration model supports per-tenant JSON overlays (logos, colors, footer)
- MFE branding configuration injection working (reads SiteConfiguration at runtime)

## Non-goals
- Provisioning script (Phase 1)
- Actual tenant creation (Phase 1)
- Cross-tenant isolation tests (Phase 1)
- External client onboarding (Phase 2)

## Constraints
- Must NOT break existing single-tenant Mereka Academy functionality
- Redis namespace format must follow enterprise:{uuid}:{key_type}:{key_id}
- ClickHouse column must be nullable (existing events have no UUID)
- Feature flags default to False (explicit opt-in per tenant)

## Plan
1. Configure EnterpriseCustomer model extension in LMS settings (site_id FK mapping)
2. Implement Redis cache key namespacing middleware
3. Add enterprise_customer_uuid column to ClickHouse xAPI events table
4. Implement xAPI event tagging with enterprise_customer_uuid in event producer
5. Create feature flags in LMS settings (ENABLE_MULTI_TENANT_BRANDING, ENABLE_TENANT_ANALYTICS_SCOPING)
6. Create tenant branding directory: infrastructure/tutor/themes/mereka/tenants/
7. Configure SiteConfiguration for per-tenant JSON overlays
8. Implement MFE branding configuration injection from SiteConfiguration
9. Add Prometheus metrics: tenant_request_total{tenant_uuid}, tenant_cache_hit_ratio{tenant_uuid}
10. Create verification script scripts/qa/verify-tenant-foundation.sh

## AC (Given/When/Then)
- Given EnterpriseCustomer with site_id FK, When Django resolves request to Site, Then correct SiteConfiguration loads for that tenant
- Given Redis cache with namespaced keys, When tenant A writes cache, Then tenant B reads return empty (no cross-contamination)
- Given xAPI event produced by tenant learner, When event stored in ClickHouse, Then enterprise_customer_uuid column is populated
- Given ENABLE_MULTI_TENANT_BRANDING=False, When tenant domain is visited, Then default Mereka branding renders (no tenant override)

## Verification
scripts/qa/verify-tenant-foundation.sh (check settings, cache config, ClickHouse schema, feature flags)

## Rollback
- Remove feature flags (set to False)
- ClickHouse column is nullable — no data migration needed to rollback
- Redis namespace change is additive — old keys still work

## Observability
- Prometheus: tenant_request_total{tenant_uuid}, tenant_cache_hit_ratio{tenant_uuid}
- Loki: {app="lms"} |~ "enterprise_customer_uuid" | logfmt

## Security
- Redis namespacing prevents cross-tenant cache poisoning
- xAPI tagging enables per-tenant analytics scoping
- Feature flags gate all multi-tenant behavior (safe rollback)

## Dependencies
- Blocks: Phase 1 (Provisioning)
- Parent: mereka-lms-1gcr

## Evidence
- Git history: git log --grep='tenancy' --oneline

## Learning
- 1. Tenancy implementation follows Open edX Django app pattern (custom-apps/ + Tutor plugin registration). 2. Always create verification script alongside implementation for regression detection.

title: Libraries: Phase 3 — Scale, Search, Analytics, Backup/Recovery
description:
## Context
Libraries must scale to production load: full-text search via Meilisearch, usage analytics, backup/recovery, and load testing at 500+ libraries with 50K+ components. Without scale testing, library operations may degrade under real multi-tenant usage and there is no disaster recovery path for library content.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC-LIB-020: Listing API returns results in <500ms p95 with 500 libraries and 50K components
- [ ] AC-LIB-021: Search query "python basics" returns matching library components in <2s
- [ ] AC-LIB-022: Usage report for library used in 15 courses shows all 15 references
- [ ] AC-LIB-023: Disaster recovery restore from backup restores all libraries and components intact
- [ ] AC-LIB-024: Nightly OLX exports complete for all libraries without errors
- [ ] AC-LIB-025: No data loss during backup/restore cycle (component count matches pre/post)

## Verification
- \`scripts/qa/verify-libraries-scale.sh\`
- \`scripts/qa/load-test-libraries.sh --libraries=500 --components=50000\`
- \`kubectl get cronjob -n mereka-lms | grep library-export\`
- Release Blocking: \`scripts/qa/verify-libraries-scale.sh\`

## Outcome
- Libraries performant at 500-library / 50K-component scale
- Full-text search returns results in under 2 seconds
- Backup/recovery path validated — zero data loss during DR drill

## Negative Assertions
- [ ] AC-NEG-LIB-010: Load test MUST NOT run against production data — synthetic libraries only
- [ ] AC-NEG-LIB-011: Backup MUST NOT include soft-deleted libraries past retention period
- [ ] AC-NEG-LIB-012: Restore MUST NOT overwrite libraries modified after backup timestamp

## Evidence
- \`verify-libraries-scale.sh\` output; load test latency report; backup/restore component count comparison; CronJob status

## Rollback
- Load test: delete synthetic libraries after test completion
- Backup CronJob: \`kubectl delete cronjob library-export -n mereka-lms\`
- Restore: backup is non-destructive — original data preserved

## Risk
- P1 — 50K-component load test may exhaust Meilisearch memory; mitigated by dedicated Meilisearch instance with 4GB+ RAM
- P2 — backup storage costs grow linearly; mitigated by retention policy with automatic pruning

title: Fix production kustomize apply drift
description:
Kubectl apply for production overlay fails on GKE due to selector immutability and caddy port drift.

Errors observed:
- Deployments: selector immutable when apply tries to add or remove environment label.
- Service caddy: spec.ports[1].name required (likely mismatch with live http3 port plus last-applied state).

Goal:
- Make production overlay apply cleanly without touching selectors (labels transformer with includeSelectors false or remove env label),
- Reconcile caddy service ports to match live service (http/https/http3),
- Avoid deleting PVCs or scaling DB workloads to 0.

Acceptance:
- kubectl apply -k deploy/k8s/overlays/production succeeds on GKE,
- No selector immutability errors,
- Caddy service update applies cleanly.

title: Auth hardening: OIDC provider config cleanup strategy (ConfigurationModel duplicates)

- scripts/shared/multisite_bootstrap_django.py creating a new enabled row when latest is disabled
- scripts/qa/verify-oidc-provider-configs.sh asserting latest row enabled/visible

Remaining work:

- If we don't delete, document the expected growth and add a guardrail to prevent creating new rows when not needed.

Acceptance:
- Documented cleanup policy and operational runbook entry in docs/operations/AUTH_AND_PERMISSIONS.md.
- Optional: add a safe archive approach if deletion not allowed.
close_reason: OIDC cleanup policy documented in AUTH_AND_PERMISSIONS.md. Policy: don't delete old rows (audit trail), monitor quarterly, investigate >20 rows/site. Bootstrap script handles recovery.
